        return Print(value, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def if_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        cond = self.expression()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def while_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        cond = self.expression()
        return While(cond, self.block(), line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def for_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("in")
        iterable = self.expression()
        return For(name.text, iterable, self.block(), line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def return_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        value = None if self.at(";") else self.expression()
        self.end_statement()
        return Return(value, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def jump_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        self.end_statement()
        kind = Break if tok.text == "break" else Continue
        return kind(line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def fn_decl(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        params, ret, body = self.function_rest()
        return Fn(name.text, params, ret, body, line=name.line, col=name.col)

    def function_expr(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        params, ret, body = self.function_rest()
        return FnExpr(params, ret, body, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def function_rest(self):
        """What follows 'fn' or 'fn name': parameters, return type, body."""
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = self.annotation("->")
        return params, ret, self.block()

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        return (name.text, self.annotation(":"))

    def block(self):
        tok = self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error(f"expected '}}' to close the block opened at {tok.line}:{tok.col}, "
                                 f"found end of input")
            stmt = self.declaration()
            if stmt is not None:
                stmts.append(stmt)
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def simple_stmt(self):
        """An assignment (to a name or an index) or an expression statement."""
        expr = self.expression()
        if self.at("="):
            eq = self.advance()
            value = self.expression()
            self.end_statement()
            if isinstance(expr, Var):
                return Assign(expr.name, value, line=expr.line, col=expr.col)
            if isinstance(expr, Index):
                return SetIndex(expr.target, expr.index, value, line=expr.line, col=expr.col)
            # The statement itself was well formed, so report without panicking.
            self.errors.append(self.error("can only assign to a name or an index", eq))
            return None
        self.end_statement()
        return ExprStmt(expr, line=expr.line, col=expr.col)


def parse_expression(source):
    """One expression and nothing after it. Raises the first LexError or ParseError."""
    parser = Parser(tokenize(source))
    expr = parser.expression()
    if parser.peek().kind != "EOF":
        raise parser.error(f"expected end of input, found {describe(parser.peek())}")
    return expr


def parse(source):
    """(program, errors). If the lexer found mistakes, errors are the lexer's
    and program is None: parsing broken tokens only adds confusing errors.
    Otherwise errors are the parser's, and the program must not run unless
    there are none."""
    tokens, errors = Lexer(source).scan()
    if errors:
        return None, errors
    parser = Parser(tokens)
    program = parser.program()
    return program, parser.errors


def quote(text):
    """A string as Comet source writes it: in quotes, with its escapes."""
    return '"' + text.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n") + '"'


def group(head, *parts):
    return "(" + " ".join([head, *parts]) + ")"


def sexpr(node):
    """The tree as a prefix expression, for tests and debugging:
    1 + 2 * x becomes (+ 1 (* 2 x))."""
    if isinstance(node, Num):
        return str(node.value)
    if isinstance(node, Str):
        return quote(node.value)
    if isinstance(node, Bool):
        return "true" if node.value else "false"
    if isinstance(node, Nil):
        return "nil"
    if isinstance(node, Var):
        return node.name
    if isinstance(node, Unary):
        return group(node.op, sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, Binary):
        return group(node.op, sexpr(node.left), sexpr(node.right))
    if isinstance(node, Call):
        return group("call", sexpr(node.callee), *map(sexpr, node.args))
    if isinstance(node, Index):
        return group("index", sexpr(node.target), sexpr(node.index))
    if isinstance(node, ListLit):
        return group("list", *map(sexpr, node.items))
    if isinstance(node, MapLit):
        return group("map", *[sexpr(part) for pair in node.pairs for part in pair])
    return sexpr_statement(node)


def sexpr_statement(node):
    """sexpr for statements and functions: (let x 1), (block ...), ..."""
    if isinstance(node, (Fn, FnExpr)):
        params = "(" + " ".join(name for name, _type in node.params) + ")"
        head = ["fn", node.name] if isinstance(node, Fn) else ["fn"]
        return group(*head, params, sexpr(node.body))
    if isinstance(node, Let):
        return group("let", node.name, sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, Assign):
        return group("set", node.name, sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, SetIndex):
        return group("set", group("index", sexpr(node.target), sexpr(node.index)), sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, Print):
        return group("print", sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, ExprStmt):
        return group("expr", sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, If):
        parts = [sexpr(node.cond), sexpr(node.then)]
        if node.else_ is not None:
            parts.append(sexpr(node.else_))
        return group("if", *parts)
    if isinstance(node, While):
        return group("while", sexpr(node.cond), sexpr(node.body))
    if isinstance(node, For):
        return group("for", node.name, sexpr(node.iterable), sexpr(node.body))
    if isinstance(node, Break):
        return "(break)"
    if isinstance(node, Continue):
        return "(continue)"
    if isinstance(node, Return):
        return "(return)" if node.expr is None else group("return", sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, Block):
        return group("block", *map(sexpr, node.stmts))
    if isinstance(node, Program):
        return group("program", *map(sexpr, node.stmts))
    raise TypeError(f"sexpr cannot show {type(node).__name__}")


# ============================================================================
# Values
# ============================================================================

class CometError(Exception):
    """A runtime error in the Comet program (not a bug in the interpreter)."""


def comet_div(a, b):
    """Integer division that rounds toward zero, like C."""
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def type_name(value):
    """Comet's name for a value's type."""
    if value is None:
        return "nil"
    if isinstance(value, bool):     # before int: in Python, True is an int
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return "str"
    raise TypeError(f"not a Comet value: {value!r}")


def repr_value(value):
    """A value as Comet source writes it: strings in quotes."""
    if value is None:
        return "nil"
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return str(value)
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return quote(value)
    raise TypeError(f"not a Comet value: {value!r}")


def show(value):
    """What print writes: a string as it is, anything else as repr_value."""
    return value if isinstance(value, str) else repr_value(value)


def values_equal(a, b):
    """Comet's ==: values of different types are never equal."""
    if type_name(a) != type_name(b):
        return False
    return a == b    # same Comet type, so Python's == is right (fns: the same fn)


ARITHMETIC = {
    "+": operator.add, "-": operator.sub, "*": operator.mul, "/": comet_div, "%": comet_mod,
    "<": operator.lt, "<=": operator.le, ">": operator.gt, ">=": operator.ge,
}
ORDERING = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=")
JOINABLE = ("str",)             # + also joins two of these


def arithmetic(op, left, right):
    """+ - * / % < <= > >= with Comet's type rules."""
    lt, rt = type_name(left), type_name(right)
    if lt == rt == "int":
        return ARITHMETIC[op](left, right)
    if op == "+" and lt == rt and lt in JOINABLE:
        return left + right
    if op in ORDERING and lt == rt == "str":
        return ARITHMETIC[op](left, right)
    raise CometError(f"'{op}' cannot combine {lt} and {rt}")


class Closure:
    """A Comet function value: its declaration (an Fn or FnExpr node) and
    the Environment it was made in, which it keeps alive."""

    def __init__(self, decl, env):
        self.decl = decl
        self.env = env

    @property
    def name(self):
        return self.decl.name if isinstance(self.decl, Fn) else None

    def label(self):
        return self.name or "anonymous fn"


class ReturnSignal(Exception):
    """Carries a return value up to the call waiting for it. Not a
    CometError, so nothing a Comet program does can catch it."""

    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value


# ============================================================================
# The interpreter
# ============================================================================


class Environment:
    """One scope's variables, and the scope around it (None for the globals)."""

    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        if self.parent is not None and name in self.values:
            raise CometError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.values[name] = value

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env.values[name]
            env = env.parent
        raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                env.values[name] = value
                return
            env = env.parent
        raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {name}")


class Interpreter:
    """Runs a syntax tree. Printed lines collect in self.output."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.env = self.globals       # the scope running now
        self.output = []

    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def handler(self, prefix, node):
        """The method for this kind of node: exec_Print for a Print, and so on."""
        method = getattr(self, prefix + type(node).__name__, None)
        if method is None:
            raise CometError(f"{type(node).__name__} is not supported yet")
        return method

    def execute(self, stmt):
        self.handler("exec_", stmt)(stmt)

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        return self.handler("eval_", expr)(expr)

    def execute_block(self, stmts, env):
        """Runs stmts with env as the current scope, and always puts the old
        scope back, also when a statement raises."""
        previous = self.env
        self.env = env
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.execute(stmt)
        finally:
            self.env = previous

    # ---- statements ----

    def exec_Let(self, stmt):
        self.env.define(stmt.name, self.evaluate(stmt.expr))

    def exec_Assign(self, stmt):
        value = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        self.env.assign(stmt.name, value)

    def exec_Print(self, stmt):
        self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))

    def exec_ExprStmt(self, stmt):
        self.evaluate(stmt.expr)

    def exec_If(self, stmt):
        if self.condition(stmt.cond):
            self.execute(stmt.then)
        elif stmt.else_ is not None:
            self.execute(stmt.else_)    # a Block, or an If for "else if"

    def exec_While(self, stmt):
        while self.condition(stmt.cond):
            self.execute(stmt.body)

    def exec_Block(self, stmt):
        self.execute_block(stmt.stmts, Environment(self.env))

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"a condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    # ---- expressions ----

    def eval_Num(self, expr):
        return expr.value

    eval_Str = eval_Bool = eval_Num

    def eval_Nil(self, expr):
        return None

    def eval_Var(self, expr):
        return self.env.lookup(expr.name)

    def eval_Unary(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
        if expr.op == "-":
            self.need("int", value, "-")
            return -value
        self.need("bool", value, "not")
        return not value

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def eval_Binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if left == (op == "or"):     # false and ..., true or ...: already decided
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            lt, rt = type_name(left), type_name(right)
            if lt != rt and "nil" not in (lt, rt):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {lt} with {rt}")
            return values_equal(left, right) == (op == "==")
        return arithmetic(op, left, right)

    # Write exec_Fn, eval_FnExpr, exec_Return, eval_Call and call(callee, args).


def run(source):
    """Runs a Comet program and returns what it printed, one line per print.
    Errors found before running are the whole answer; a runtime error is
    added after whatever was printed before it."""
    program, errors = parse(source)
    if errors:
        return "\n".join(str(e) for e in errors)
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(program)
    except CometError as e:
        interp.output.append(f"runtime error: {e}")
    return "\n".join(interp.output)
--- solution
"""Comet: a small programming language, built in layers.

    source text -> Lexer -> tokens -> Parser -> syntax tree
                -> Resolver -> Interpreter -> printed output

Each layer only talks to the one after it, so each can be tested alone.
"""
import operator
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


# ============================================================================
# Tokens and the lexer
# ============================================================================

KEYWORDS = {
    "let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "for", "in", "break",
    "continue", "print", "true", "false", "nil", "and", "or", "not",
}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){}[],;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = set("0123456789")
LETTERS = set("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_")
# Characters people type from other languages, and what Comet wants instead.
LEX_HINTS = {
    "'": "strings use double quotes",
    "&": "use 'and'",
    "|": "use 'or'",
    "!": "use 'not', or '!=' for not equal",
}


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str   # NUMBER, STRING, IDENT, KEYWORD, OP or EOF
    text: str   # the source text; for a STRING, the decoded value
    line: int   # counted from 1
    col: int    # counted from 1


class StaticError(Exception):
    """A mistake found before the program runs. Prints as "line:col: message"."""

    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.message = message
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


class LexError(StaticError):
    """A character sequence that is not a Comet token."""


class Lexer:
    """Turns source text into tokens. It keeps going after a mistake, so one
    scan reports every lexing error, each with its line and column."""

    def __init__(self, source):
        self.source = source
        self.pos = 0          # index of the next character to read
        self.line = 1         # where that character is, for messages
        self.col = 1
        self.tokens = []
        self.errors = []

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        """A character ahead of the read position, or "" past the end."""
        i = self.pos + ahead
        return self.source[i] if i < len(self.source) else ""

    def advance(self):
        """Consumes one character and keeps line and col in step with it."""
        ch = self.source[self.pos]
        self.pos += 1
        if ch == "\n":
            self.line += 1
            self.col = 1
        else:
            self.col += 1
        return ch

    def scan(self):
        """Returns (tokens, errors): every token ending with EOF, and every LexError."""
        while self.pos < len(self.source):
            self.scan_token()
        self.tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", self.line, self.col))
        return self.tokens, self.errors

    def scan_token(self):
        line, col = self.line, self.col
        ch = self.peek()
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            self.advance()
        elif ch == "#":
            while self.peek() not in ("", "\n"):
                self.advance()
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            self.number(line, col)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            self.word(line, col)
        elif ch == '"':
            self.string(line, col)
        elif ch + self.peek(1) in TWO_CHAR:
            text = self.advance() + self.advance()
            self.tokens.append(Token("OP", text, line, col))
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            self.tokens.append(Token("OP", self.advance(), line, col))
        else:
            self.advance()   # skip it, report it, and carry on
            message = f"unexpected character {ch!r}"
            if ch in LEX_HINTS:
                message += f" ({LEX_HINTS[ch]})"
            self.errors.append(LexError(message, line, col))

    def number(self, line, col):
        start = self.pos
        while self.peek() in DIGITS:
            self.advance()
        self.tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", self.source[start:self.pos], line, col))

    def word(self, line, col):
        start = self.pos
        while self.peek() in LETTERS or self.peek() in DIGITS:
            self.advance()
        text = self.source[start:self.pos]
        kind = "KEYWORD" if text in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
        self.tokens.append(Token(kind, text, line, col))

    def string(self, line, col):
        """A string literal. The token's text is the decoded value."""
        self.advance()  # the opening quote
        chars = []
        while True:
            ch = self.peek()
            if ch in ("", "\n"):
                # Strings never span lines, so the rest of this line is lost.
                self.errors.append(LexError("unterminated string", line, col))
                return
            if ch == '"':
                self.advance()
                break
            if ch == "\\":
                at_line, at_col = self.line, self.col
                self.advance()
                code = self.peek()
                if code in ESCAPES:
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[self.advance()])
                elif code not in ("", "\n"):
                    self.advance()
                    self.errors.append(LexError(f"unknown escape \\{code}", at_line, at_col))
                continue
            chars.append(self.advance())
        self.tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), line, col))


def tokenize(source):
    """The tokens of source; raises the first LexError if there is one."""
    tokens, errors = Lexer(source).scan()
    if errors:
        raise errors[0]
    return tokens


def point_at(source, line, col):
    """Two lines: source line `line`, and a caret under column `col`.
    Tabs before the column are copied, so the caret lines up in a terminal."""
    lines = source.split("\n")
    text = lines[line - 1] if 1 <= line <= len(lines) else ""
    pad = "".join("\t" if c == "\t" else " " for c in text[:col - 1])
    return text + "\n" + pad.ljust(col - 1) + "^"


# ============================================================================
# The syntax tree
# ============================================================================

def pos_field():
    """A node's line or column: given by keyword, and never part of ==."""
    return field(default=0, kw_only=True, compare=False, repr=False)


@dataclass
class Node:
    line: int = pos_field()
    col: int = pos_field()


@dataclass
class Num(Node):
    value: int


@dataclass
class Str(Node):
    value: str


@dataclass
class Bool(Node):
    value: bool


@dataclass
class Nil(Node):
    pass


@dataclass
class Var(Node):
    name: str


@dataclass
class Unary(Node):
    op: str
    expr: Node


@dataclass
class Binary(Node):
    op: str
    left: Node
    right: Node


@dataclass
class Call(Node):
    callee: Node
    args: list


@dataclass
class Index(Node):
    target: Node
    index: Node


@dataclass
class ListLit(Node):
    items: list


@dataclass
class MapLit(Node):
    pairs: list     # (key, value) pairs of expressions


@dataclass
class FnExpr(Node):
    params: list    # (name, type) pairs; type is None without an annotation
    ret: object
    body: object    # a Block


@dataclass
class Let(Node):
    name: str
    type: object
    expr: Node


@dataclass
class Assign(Node):
    name: str
    expr: Node


@dataclass
class SetIndex(Node):
    target: Node
    index: Node
    expr: Node


@dataclass
class Print(Node):
    expr: Node


@dataclass
class If(Node):
    cond: Node
    then: object
    else_: object   # None, a Block, or an If (for "else if")


@dataclass
class While(Node):
    cond: Node
    body: object


@dataclass
class For(Node):
    name: str
    iterable: Node
    body: object


@dataclass
class Break(Node):
    pass


@dataclass
class Continue(Node):
    pass


@dataclass
class Fn(Node):
    name: str
    params: list
    ret: object
    body: object


@dataclass
class Return(Node):
    expr: object    # None for a bare "return;"


@dataclass
class ExprStmt(Node):
    expr: Node


@dataclass
class Block(Node):
    stmts: list


@dataclass
class Program(Node):
    stmts: list


# ============================================================================
# The parser
# ============================================================================

class ParseError(StaticError):
    """Tokens in an order the grammar does not allow."""


def describe(tok):
    """How a token is named in an error message."""
    if tok.kind == "EOF":
        return "end of input"
    if tok.kind == "STRING":
        return "a string"
    return f"'{tok.text}'"


# Binding powers, weakest first. An operator with a higher power takes its
# operands before an operator with a lower power does.
LOWEST, OR, AND, NOT, COMPARE, SUM, PRODUCT, UNARY, POSTFIX = range(9)
COMPARISONS = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
INFIX = {
    "or": OR, "and": AND,
    "==": COMPARE, "!=": COMPARE, "<": COMPARE, "<=": COMPARE, ">": COMPARE, ">=": COMPARE,
    "+": SUM, "-": SUM,
    "*": PRODUCT, "/": PRODUCT, "%": PRODUCT,
    "(": POSTFIX, "[": POSTFIX,
}
STATEMENT_START = ("let", "fn", "if", "while", "for", "return", "print", "break", "continue")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str", "list", "map", "any")


class Parser:
    """A Pratt parser for expressions, and recursive descent for statements."""

    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0
        self.errors = []      # every ParseError found so far

    def peek(self):
        return self.tokens[self.pos]

    def at(self, *texts):
        """Is the next token one of these operators or keywords?"""
        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        """Consumes the next token and returns it. EOF is never consumed."""
        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message, tok=None):
        tok = tok or self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}', found {describe(self.peek())}")
        return self.advance()

    # ---- expressions: the Pratt loop -------------------------------------

    def expression(self, power=LOWEST):
        """An expression whose operators all bind more tightly than `power`."""
        left = self.prefix()
        while True:
            tok = self.peek()
            op_power = INFIX.get(tok.text, LOWEST) if tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") else LOWEST
            if op_power <= power:
                return left
            left = self.infix(left, op_power)

    def prefix(self):
        """Something that can start an expression."""
        tok = self.peek()
        where = dict(line=tok.line, col=tok.col)
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text), **where)
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text, **where)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text, **where)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true", **where)
        if self.at("nil"):
            self.advance()
            return Nil(**where)
        if self.at("-", "not"):
            self.advance()
            operand = self.expression(UNARY if tok.text == "-" else NOT)
            return Unary(tok.text, operand, **where)
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expression()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        if self.at("["):
            self.advance()
            return ListLit(self.items("]"), **where)
        if self.at("{"):
            self.advance()
            return MapLit(self.pairs(), **where)
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.function_expr()
        raise self.error(f"expected an expression, found {describe(tok)}")

    def infix(self, left, power):
        """An operator after a complete left operand, and what it needs after it."""
        tok = self.advance()
        where = dict(line=tok.line, col=tok.col)
        if tok.text == "(":
            return Call(left, self.items(")"), line=left.line, col=left.col)
        if tok.text == "[":
            index = self.expression()
            self.expect("]")
            return Index(left, index, **where)
        # A binary operator. The right side may only hold operators that bind
        # more tightly, so a second operator of the same power ends it: that
        # is what makes 10 - 3 - 2 group as (10 - 3) - 2.
        node = Binary(tok.text, left, self.expression(power), **where)
        if tok.text in COMPARISONS and self.at(*COMPARISONS):
            raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return node

    def items(self, close):
        """Comma-separated expressions up to `close`, which is consumed."""
        items = []
        if not self.at(close):
            items.append(self.expression())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                items.append(self.expression())
        self.expect(close)
        return items

    def pairs(self):
        """The key: value pairs of a map literal, up to and including '}'."""
        pairs = []
        if not self.at("}"):
            pairs.append(self.pair())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                pairs.append(self.pair())
        self.expect("}")
        return pairs

    def pair(self):
        key = self.expression()
        self.expect(":")
        return (key, self.expression())

    # ---- statements, with error recovery ---------------------------------

    def program(self):
        """Every statement up to EOF. Errors are collected in self.errors and
        parsing goes on after each one, so one pass reports them all."""
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmt = self.declaration()
            if stmt is not None:
                stmts.append(stmt)
        return Program(stmts)

    def declaration(self):
        """One statement. After a syntax error it records the error, skips to
        a safe place, and returns None."""
        start = self.pos
        try:
            return self.statement()
        except ParseError as e:
            self.errors.append(e)
            self.synchronize(start)
            return None

    def synchronize(self, start):
        """Panic mode: skip to just after a ';', or to a token that starts a
        statement, or to a '}' (so the block around us can close). A block
        entered while skipping is skipped whole, up to its own '}'. Always
        moves at least one token, so parsing cannot get stuck."""
        depth = 0
        if self.pos == start:
            depth = self.skip(depth)
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            if depth == 0:
                before = self.tokens[self.pos - 1]
                if before.kind == "OP" and before.text == ";":
                    return
                if self.at(*STATEMENT_START) or self.at("}"):
                    return
            depth = self.skip(depth)

    def skip(self, depth):
        """Consumes one token while recovering; returns the new block depth."""
        tok = self.advance()
        if tok.kind == "OP" and tok.text == "{":
            return depth + 1
        if tok.kind == "OP" and tok.text == "}" and depth > 0:
            return depth - 1
        return depth

    def statement(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "KEYWORD":
            if tok.text == "fn" and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "IDENT":
                return self.fn_decl()
            handler = {
                "let": self.let_stmt, "print": self.print_stmt, "if": self.if_stmt,
                "while": self.while_stmt, "for": self.for_stmt, "return": self.return_stmt,
                "break": self.jump_stmt, "continue": self.jump_stmt,
            }.get(tok.text)
            if handler is not None:
                return handler()
        return self.simple_stmt()

    def end_statement(self):
        self.expect(";")

    def name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error(f"expected a name, found {describe(tok)}")
        return self.advance()

    def annotation(self, marker):
        """An optional type after ':' or '->'. Nothing checks types yet; they
        are notes for the reader."""
        if not self.at(marker):
            return None
        self.advance()
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error(f"expected a type, found {describe(tok)}")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = self.annotation(":")
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expression()
        self.end_statement()
        return Let(name.text, type_, value, line=name.line, col=name.col)

    def print_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        value = self.expression()
        self.end_statement()
        return Print(value, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def if_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        cond = self.expression()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def while_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        cond = self.expression()
        return While(cond, self.block(), line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def for_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("in")
        iterable = self.expression()
        return For(name.text, iterable, self.block(), line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def return_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        value = None if self.at(";") else self.expression()
        self.end_statement()
        return Return(value, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def jump_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        self.end_statement()
        kind = Break if tok.text == "break" else Continue
        return kind(line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def fn_decl(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        params, ret, body = self.function_rest()
        return Fn(name.text, params, ret, body, line=name.line, col=name.col)

    def function_expr(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        params, ret, body = self.function_rest()
        return FnExpr(params, ret, body, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def function_rest(self):
        """What follows 'fn' or 'fn name': parameters, return type, body."""
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = self.annotation("->")
        return params, ret, self.block()

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        return (name.text, self.annotation(":"))

    def block(self):
        tok = self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error(f"expected '}}' to close the block opened at {tok.line}:{tok.col}, "
                                 f"found end of input")
            stmt = self.declaration()
            if stmt is not None:
                stmts.append(stmt)
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def simple_stmt(self):
        """An assignment (to a name or an index) or an expression statement."""
        expr = self.expression()
        if self.at("="):
            eq = self.advance()
            value = self.expression()
            self.end_statement()
            if isinstance(expr, Var):
                return Assign(expr.name, value, line=expr.line, col=expr.col)
            if isinstance(expr, Index):
                return SetIndex(expr.target, expr.index, value, line=expr.line, col=expr.col)
            # The statement itself was well formed, so report without panicking.
            self.errors.append(self.error("can only assign to a name or an index", eq))
            return None
        self.end_statement()
        return ExprStmt(expr, line=expr.line, col=expr.col)


def parse_expression(source):
    """One expression and nothing after it. Raises the first LexError or ParseError."""
    parser = Parser(tokenize(source))
    expr = parser.expression()
    if parser.peek().kind != "EOF":
        raise parser.error(f"expected end of input, found {describe(parser.peek())}")
    return expr


def parse(source):
    """(program, errors). If the lexer found mistakes, errors are the lexer's
    and program is None: parsing broken tokens only adds confusing errors.
    Otherwise errors are the parser's, and the program must not run unless
    there are none."""
    tokens, errors = Lexer(source).scan()
    if errors:
        return None, errors
    parser = Parser(tokens)
    program = parser.program()
    return program, parser.errors


def quote(text):
    """A string as Comet source writes it: in quotes, with its escapes."""
    return '"' + text.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n") + '"'


def group(head, *parts):
    return "(" + " ".join([head, *parts]) + ")"


def sexpr(node):
    """The tree as a prefix expression, for tests and debugging:
    1 + 2 * x becomes (+ 1 (* 2 x))."""
    if isinstance(node, Num):
        return str(node.value)
    if isinstance(node, Str):
        return quote(node.value)
    if isinstance(node, Bool):
        return "true" if node.value else "false"
    if isinstance(node, Nil):
        return "nil"
    if isinstance(node, Var):
        return node.name
    if isinstance(node, Unary):
        return group(node.op, sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, Binary):
        return group(node.op, sexpr(node.left), sexpr(node.right))
    if isinstance(node, Call):
        return group("call", sexpr(node.callee), *map(sexpr, node.args))
    if isinstance(node, Index):
        return group("index", sexpr(node.target), sexpr(node.index))
    if isinstance(node, ListLit):
        return group("list", *map(sexpr, node.items))
    if isinstance(node, MapLit):
        return group("map", *[sexpr(part) for pair in node.pairs for part in pair])
    return sexpr_statement(node)


def sexpr_statement(node):
    """sexpr for statements and functions: (let x 1), (block ...), ..."""
    if isinstance(node, (Fn, FnExpr)):
        params = "(" + " ".join(name for name, _type in node.params) + ")"
        head = ["fn", node.name] if isinstance(node, Fn) else ["fn"]
        return group(*head, params, sexpr(node.body))
    if isinstance(node, Let):
        return group("let", node.name, sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, Assign):
        return group("set", node.name, sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, SetIndex):
        return group("set", group("index", sexpr(node.target), sexpr(node.index)), sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, Print):
        return group("print", sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, ExprStmt):
        return group("expr", sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, If):
        parts = [sexpr(node.cond), sexpr(node.then)]
        if node.else_ is not None:
            parts.append(sexpr(node.else_))
        return group("if", *parts)
    if isinstance(node, While):
        return group("while", sexpr(node.cond), sexpr(node.body))
    if isinstance(node, For):
        return group("for", node.name, sexpr(node.iterable), sexpr(node.body))
    if isinstance(node, Break):
        return "(break)"
    if isinstance(node, Continue):
        return "(continue)"
    if isinstance(node, Return):
        return "(return)" if node.expr is None else group("return", sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, Block):
        return group("block", *map(sexpr, node.stmts))
    if isinstance(node, Program):
        return group("program", *map(sexpr, node.stmts))
    raise TypeError(f"sexpr cannot show {type(node).__name__}")


# ============================================================================
# Values
# ============================================================================

class CometError(Exception):
    """A runtime error in the Comet program (not a bug in the interpreter)."""


def comet_div(a, b):
    """Integer division that rounds toward zero, like C."""
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def type_name(value):
    """Comet's name for a value's type."""
    if value is None:
        return "nil"
    if isinstance(value, bool):     # before int: in Python, True is an int
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return "str"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return "fn"
    raise TypeError(f"not a Comet value: {value!r}")


def repr_value(value):
    """A value as Comet source writes it: strings in quotes."""
    if value is None:
        return "nil"
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return str(value)
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return quote(value)
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return f"<fn {value.name}>" if value.name else "<fn>"
    raise TypeError(f"not a Comet value: {value!r}")


def show(value):
    """What print writes: a string as it is, anything else as repr_value."""
    return value if isinstance(value, str) else repr_value(value)


def values_equal(a, b):
    """Comet's ==: values of different types are never equal."""
    if type_name(a) != type_name(b):
        return False
    return a == b    # same Comet type, so Python's == is right (fns: the same fn)


ARITHMETIC = {
    "+": operator.add, "-": operator.sub, "*": operator.mul, "/": comet_div, "%": comet_mod,
    "<": operator.lt, "<=": operator.le, ">": operator.gt, ">=": operator.ge,
}
ORDERING = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=")
JOINABLE = ("str",)             # + also joins two of these


def arithmetic(op, left, right):
    """+ - * / % < <= > >= with Comet's type rules."""
    lt, rt = type_name(left), type_name(right)
    if lt == rt == "int":
        return ARITHMETIC[op](left, right)
    if op == "+" and lt == rt and lt in JOINABLE:
        return left + right
    if op in ORDERING and lt == rt == "str":
        return ARITHMETIC[op](left, right)
    raise CometError(f"'{op}' cannot combine {lt} and {rt}")


class Closure:
    """A Comet function value: its declaration (an Fn or FnExpr node) and
    the Environment it was made in, which it keeps alive."""

    def __init__(self, decl, env):
        self.decl = decl
        self.env = env

    @property
    def name(self):
        return self.decl.name if isinstance(self.decl, Fn) else None

    def label(self):
        return self.name or "anonymous fn"


class ReturnSignal(Exception):
    """Carries a return value up to the call waiting for it. Not a
    CometError, so nothing a Comet program does can catch it."""

    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value


def check_arity(name, fewest, most, got):
    if fewest <= got <= most:
        return
    if fewest == most:
        wanted = f"{fewest} argument" + ("" if fewest == 1 else "s")
    elif most == fewest + 1:
        wanted = f"{fewest} or {most} arguments"
    else:
        wanted = f"{fewest} to {most} arguments"
    raise CometError(f"{name} expects {wanted}, got {got}")


# ============================================================================
# The interpreter
# ============================================================================


class Environment:
    """One scope's variables, and the scope around it (None for the globals)."""

    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        if self.parent is not None and name in self.values:
            raise CometError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.values[name] = value

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env.values[name]
            env = env.parent
        raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                env.values[name] = value
                return
            env = env.parent
        raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {name}")


class Interpreter:
    """Runs a syntax tree. Printed lines collect in self.output."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.env = self.globals       # the scope running now
        self.output = []

    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            try:
                self.execute(stmt)
            except ReturnSignal:
                raise CometError("return outside a function") from None

    def handler(self, prefix, node):
        """The method for this kind of node: exec_Print for a Print, and so on."""
        method = getattr(self, prefix + type(node).__name__, None)
        if method is None:
            raise CometError(f"{type(node).__name__} is not supported yet")
        return method

    def execute(self, stmt):
        self.handler("exec_", stmt)(stmt)

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        return self.handler("eval_", expr)(expr)

    def execute_block(self, stmts, env):
        """Runs stmts with env as the current scope, and always puts the old
        scope back, also when a statement raises."""
        previous = self.env
        self.env = env
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.execute(stmt)
        finally:
            self.env = previous

    # ---- statements ----

    def exec_Let(self, stmt):
        self.env.define(stmt.name, self.evaluate(stmt.expr))

    def exec_Assign(self, stmt):
        value = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        self.env.assign(stmt.name, value)

    def exec_Print(self, stmt):
        self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))

    def exec_ExprStmt(self, stmt):
        self.evaluate(stmt.expr)

    def exec_If(self, stmt):
        if self.condition(stmt.cond):
            self.execute(stmt.then)
        elif stmt.else_ is not None:
            self.execute(stmt.else_)    # a Block, or an If for "else if"

    def exec_While(self, stmt):
        while self.condition(stmt.cond):
            self.execute(stmt.body)

    def exec_Block(self, stmt):
        self.execute_block(stmt.stmts, Environment(self.env))

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"a condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    # ---- expressions ----

    def eval_Num(self, expr):
        return expr.value

    eval_Str = eval_Bool = eval_Num

    def eval_Nil(self, expr):
        return None

    def eval_Var(self, expr):
        return self.env.lookup(expr.name)

    def eval_Unary(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
        if expr.op == "-":
            self.need("int", value, "-")
            return -value
        self.need("bool", value, "not")
        return not value

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def eval_Binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if left == (op == "or"):     # false and ..., true or ...: already decided
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            lt, rt = type_name(left), type_name(right)
            if lt != rt and "nil" not in (lt, rt):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {lt} with {rt}")
            return values_equal(left, right) == (op == "==")
        return arithmetic(op, left, right)

    # ---- functions ----

    def exec_Fn(self, stmt):
        self.env.define(stmt.name, Closure(stmt, self.env))

    def eval_FnExpr(self, expr):
        return Closure(expr, self.env)

    def exec_Return(self, stmt):
        value = None if stmt.expr is None else self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        raise ReturnSignal(value)

    def eval_Call(self, expr):
        callee = self.evaluate(expr.callee)
        args = [self.evaluate(arg) for arg in expr.args]
        return self.call(callee, args)

    def call(self, callee, args):
        """Calls a function value with argument values, and returns its result."""
        if isinstance(callee, Closure):
            params = callee.decl.params
            check_arity(callee.label(), len(params), len(params), len(args))
            env = Environment(callee.env)   # inside the fn's own scope, not the caller's
            for (name, _type), value in zip(params, args):
                env.define(name, value)
            try:
                self.execute_block(callee.decl.body.stmts, env)
            except ReturnSignal as signal:
                return signal.value
            return None
        raise CometError(f"cannot call a value of type {type_name(callee)}")


def run(source):
    """Runs a Comet program and returns what it printed, one line per print.
    Errors found before running are the whole answer; a runtime error is
    added after whatever was printed before it."""
    program, errors = parse(source)
    if errors:
        return "\n".join(str(e) for e in errors)
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(program)
    except CometError as e:
        interp.output.append(f"runtime error: {e}")
    return "\n".join(interp.output)
--- hint
`exec_Fn` and `eval_FnExpr` are one line each. In `eval_Call`, evaluate `expr.callee` first, then `[self.evaluate(a) for a in expr.args]`, then call.
--- hint
In `call`, the new environment's parent must be `callee.env`, the environment the function was made in, not `self.env`. Define each `(name, _type)` of `callee.decl.params` with its argument, then run `callee.decl.body.stmts` with `self.execute_block(..., env)` inside a `try` that catches `ReturnSignal` and returns its value.
--- hint
For `Interpreter.run`, wrap each top-level `self.execute(stmt)` in a `try` that turns `ReturnSignal` into `CometError("return outside a function")`.
--- check case | Recursion: factorial and Fibonacci
run("fn fact(n) { if n < 2 { return 1; } return n * fact(n - 1); } print fact(20); fn fib(n) { if n < 2 { return n; } return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2); } print fib(15);")
=> "2432902008176640000\n610"
--- check case | The task's example: functions passed as values
run("fn twice(f, x) { return f(f(x)); } print twice(fn (n) { return n * 3; }, 2);")
=> "18"
--- check case | A closure keeps its variables alive
run("fn make_meter() { let reading = 0; return fn (step) { reading = reading + step; return reading; }; } let m = make_meter(); m(5); print m(2); let other = make_meter(); print other(1); print m(0);")

+++ practice | Closures in a tuple language
--- task
A small functional language writes programs as tuples:

- `("num", n)`, `("var", name)`, `("add", a, b)`;
- `("lambda", [params], body)`: a function value;
- `("call", f, [args])`: call the value of `f` with the values of `args`;
- `("let", name, value, body)`: evaluate `value`, then evaluate `body` with `name` bound to it.

Write `evaluate(expr)` that returns the value: an int, or a function value (any object you like). Functions use lexical scope: a lambda's body sees the variables that were visible where the lambda was written. Looking up a name that is not bound raises `NameError`, and calling with the wrong number of arguments raises `TypeError`.

For example, `evaluate(("let", "k", ("num", 5), ("call", ("lambda", ["x"], ("add", ("var", "x"), ("var", "k"))), [("num", 1)])))` is 6.
--- starter
def evaluate(expr):
    return 0
--- solution
class Closure:
    def __init__(self, params, body, env):
        self.params = params
        self.body = body
        self.env = env


def evaluate(expr, env=None):
    env = env or {}
    kind = expr[0]
    if kind == "num":
        return expr[1]
    if kind == "var":
        if expr[1] not in env:
            raise NameError(expr[1])
        return env[expr[1]]
    if kind == "add":
        return evaluate(expr[1], env) + evaluate(expr[2], env)
    if kind == "lambda":
        return Closure(expr[1], expr[2], env)
    if kind == "let":
        inner = dict(env)
        inner[expr[1]] = evaluate(expr[2], env)
        return evaluate(expr[3], inner)
    f = evaluate(expr[1], env)
    args = [evaluate(a, env) for a in expr[2]]
    if len(args) != len(f.params):
        raise TypeError(f"expected {len(f.params)} arguments, got {len(args)}")
    inner = dict(f.env)
    inner.update(zip(f.params, args))
    return evaluate(f.body, inner)
--- hint
Pass an environment (a dictionary) down through the evaluation. A lambda evaluates to an object holding its parameters, its body and the environment at that moment.
--- hint
A call extends the **lambda's** environment with the parameters, not the caller's. Copying the dictionary (`dict(env)`) before adding names keeps outer scopes unchanged, since nothing in this language assigns.
--- check case | The example
evaluate(("let", "k", ("num", 5), ("call", ("lambda", ["x"], ("add", ("var", "x"), ("var", "k"))), [("num", 1)])))
=> 6
--- check case | A function returned from a function remembers its argument
evaluate(("let", "adder", ("lambda", ["n"], ("lambda", ["x"], ("add", ("var", "x"), ("var", "n")))), ("call", ("call", ("var", "adder"), [("num", 10)]), [("num", 32)])))
=> 42
--- check case | Lexical, not dynamic: the caller's x is not seen
evaluate(("let", "x", ("num", 1), ("let", "f", ("lambda", [], ("var", "x")), ("let", "x", ("num", 100), ("call", ("var", "f"), [])))))
=> 1
--- check test | Unbound names and wrong argument counts
raises(NameError, lambda: evaluate(("var", "nope"))) and raises(TypeError, lambda: evaluate(("call", ("lambda", ["a"], ("var", "a")), []))) and raises(NameError, lambda: evaluate(("call", ("lambda", [], ("var", "a")), [])))

+++ practice | Lexical and dynamic scope, side by side
--- task
Write `run(program, dynamic)` for this tiny language. A program is a list of statements run in order in one global dictionary:

- `("def", name, [params], body)` defines a function, where `body` is an expression;
- `("set", name, expr)` sets a global;
- `("print", expr)` appends the value to the output list.

Expressions are `("num", n)`, `("var", name)`, `("add", a, b)`, `("call", name, [args])` and `("local", name, value, body)`, which evaluates `body` with `name` bound to `value` in a new scope.

Functions are defined at the top level only. A call makes a new scope with the parameters, whose parent is the **globals** when `dynamic` is `False` (lexical scope), or the **caller's** scope when `dynamic` is `True`. Names are looked up from the innermost scope outwards. Return the output list.
--- starter
def run(program, dynamic):
    return []
--- solution
class Scope:
    def __init__(self, values, parent):
        self.values = values
        self.parent = parent

    def lookup(self, name):
        scope = self
        while scope is not None:
            if name in scope.values:
                return scope.values[name]
            scope = scope.parent
        raise NameError(name)


def run(program, dynamic):
    globals_ = Scope({}, None)
    functions = {}
    output = []

    def ev(expr, scope):
        kind = expr[0]
        if kind == "num":
            return expr[1]
        if kind == "var":
            return scope.lookup(expr[1])
        if kind == "add":
            return ev(expr[1], scope) + ev(expr[2], scope)
        if kind == "local":
            return ev(expr[3], Scope({expr[1]: ev(expr[2], scope)}, scope))
        params, body = functions[expr[1]]
        args = [ev(a, scope) for a in expr[2]]
        parent = scope if dynamic else globals_
        return ev(body, Scope(dict(zip(params, args)), parent))

    for stmt in program:
        if stmt[0] == "def":
            functions[stmt[1]] = (stmt[2], stmt[3])
        elif stmt[0] == "set":
            globals_.values[stmt[1]] = ev(stmt[2], globals_)
        else:
            output.append(ev(stmt[1], globals_))
    return output
--- hint
Give each scope a dictionary and a parent, and look names up by walking the parents. The only difference between the two modes is one line: which scope becomes the parent of a call's new scope.
--- hint
`local` makes a scope whose parent is the current scope, in both modes.
--- check test | The classic program gives different answers
(lambda p: run(p, False) == [101] and run(p, True) == [1000])([("set", "x", ("num", 100)), ("def", "f", ["y"], ("add", ("var", "x"), ("var", "y"))), ("def", "g", [], ("local", "x", ("num", 999), ("call", "f", [("num", 1)]))), ("print", ("call", "g", []))])
--- check test | When no names clash, both modes agree
(lambda p: run(p, False) == run(p, True) == [7])([("def", "add", ["a", "b"], ("add", ("var", "a"), ("var", "b"))), ("print", ("call", "add", [("num", 3), ("num", 4)]))])
--- check test | A parameter shadows a global in both modes
(lambda p: run(p, False) == run(p, True) == [5, 1])([("set", "n", ("num", 1)), ("def", "id", ["n"], ("var", "n")), ("print", ("call", "id", [("num", 5)])), ("print", ("var", "n"))])
--- check test | Under lexical scope, a caller's local is invisible
raises(NameError, lambda: run([("def", "peek", [], ("var", "secret")), ("print", ("local", "secret", ("num", 1), ("call", "peek", [])))], False)) and run([("def", "peek", [], ("var", "secret")), ("print", ("local", "secret", ("num", 1), ("call", "peek", [])))], True) == [1]

+++ practice | Returning from deep inside
--- task
Write `call(fn, args)` for a small statement language. `fn` is a pair `(params, body)`, and `body` is a list of statements:

- `("set", name, expr)` assigns in the function's single scope;
- `("while", cond, [stmts])` loops while `cond` is true;
- `("if", cond, [stmts])` runs the statements when `cond` is true;
- `("return", expr)` ends the call at once with the value.

Expressions are `("num", n)`, `("var", name)`, `("add", a, b)`, `("mul", a, b)` and `("lt", a, b)` (a bool). A body that ends without `return` gives `None`. Implement `return` with an exception of your own, so that it leaves any number of loops and ifs at once.

For example, the function `(["n"], [("set", "i", ("num", 1)), ("while", ("lt", ("var", "i"), ("num", 100)), [("if", ("lt", ("var", "n"), ("mul", ("var", "i"), ("var", "i"))), [("return", ("var", "i"))]), ("set", "i", ("add", ("var", "i"), ("num", 1)))])])` returns the smallest `i` whose square is more than `n`: `call(fn, [10])` is 4.
--- starter
def call(fn, args):
    return None
--- solution
class Returned(Exception):
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value


def call(fn, args):
    params, body = fn
    env = dict(zip(params, args))

    def ev(e):
        kind = e[0]
        if kind == "num":
            return e[1]
        if kind == "var":
            return env[e[1]]
        a, b = ev(e[1]), ev(e[2])
        return a + b if kind == "add" else a * b if kind == "mul" else a < b

    def run(stmts):
        for s in stmts:
            if s[0] == "set":
                env[s[1]] = ev(s[2])
            elif s[0] == "while":
                while ev(s[1]):
                    run(s[2])
            elif s[0] == "if":
                if ev(s[1]):
                    run(s[2])
            else:
                raise Returned(ev(s[1]))

    try:
        run(body)
    except Returned as r:
        return r.value
    return None
--- hint
Write `run(stmts)` for statement lists, calling itself for the bodies of `while` and `if`. `return` raises your exception holding the value.
--- hint
Only `call` catches the exception: every loop and `if` in between is left automatically as it passes through.
--- check test | The example
call((["n"], [("set", "i", ("num", 1)), ("while", ("lt", ("var", "i"), ("num", 100)), [("if", ("lt", ("var", "n"), ("mul", ("var", "i"), ("var", "i"))), [("return", ("var", "i"))]), ("set", "i", ("add", ("var", "i"), ("num", 1)))])]), [10]) == 4
--- check test | No return gives None, and a return at the very start works
call(([], [("set", "a", ("num", 1))]), []) is None and call((["x"], [("return", ("add", ("var", "x"), ("num", 1))), ("set", "x", ("num", 0))]), [41]) == 42
--- check test | A return two loops deep
call(([], [("set", "i", ("num", 0)), ("while", ("lt", ("var", "i"), ("num", 5)), [("set", "j", ("num", 0)), ("while", ("lt", ("var", "j"), ("num", 5)), [("if", ("lt", ("num", 11), ("mul", ("var", "i"), ("var", "j"))), [("return", ("mul", ("var", "i"), ("num", 10)))]), ("set", "j", ("add", ("var", "j"), ("num", 1)))]), ("set", "i", ("add", ("var", "i"), ("num", 1)))])]), []) == 30
--- check source | Uses an exception class for return
class\s+\w+\(\s*Exception\s*\)

+++ practice | Binding arguments to parameters
--- task
Write `bind_args(params, args)` that matches a call's arguments to a function's parameters and returns a dict from name to value. Each entry of `params` is either a name (a required parameter) or a pair `(name, default)` (an optional one); required parameters always come first. Arguments fill parameters in order; optional parameters with no argument get their default.

Raise `TypeError` with exactly these messages:
- `missing argument NAME` for the first required parameter with no argument;
- `expected at most N arguments, got M` when there are too many.

For example, `bind_args(["a", ("b", 10)], [1])` is `{"a": 1, "b": 10}`.
--- starter
def bind_args(params, args):
    return dict(zip(params, args))
--- solution
def bind_args(params, args):
    if len(args) > len(params):
        raise TypeError(f"expected at most {len(params)} arguments, got {len(args)}")
    bound = {}
    for i, param in enumerate(params):
        name, default, required = (param, None, True) if isinstance(param, str) else (param[0], param[1], False)
        if i < len(args):
            bound[name] = args[i]
        elif required:
            raise TypeError(f"missing argument {name}")
        else:
            bound[name] = default
    return bound
--- hint
Check "too many" first, since it does not depend on which parameters are optional. Then walk the parameters with their index: use the argument if there is one, the default if the parameter has one, and otherwise report the missing name.
--- hint
Tell the two kinds of entry apart with `isinstance(param, str)`.
--- check case | The example
bind_args(["a", ("b", 10)], [1])
=> {"a": 1, "b": 10}
--- check case | Every argument given, and no parameters at all
(bind_args(["a", ("b", 10)], [1, 2]), bind_args([], []))
=> ({"a": 1, "b": 2}, {})
--- check case | Defaults that are falsy are still used
bind_args([("flag", False), ("n", 0), ("s", None)], [])
=> {"flag": False, "n": 0, "s": None}
--- check test | Missing and extra arguments
__import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(TypeError, "^missing argument b$", bind_args, ["a", "b", ("c", 1)], [1]) is None and __import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(TypeError, "^expected at most 2 arguments, got 3$", bind_args, ["a", ("b", 1)], [1, 2, 3]) is None and __import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(TypeError, "^missing argument a$", bind_args, ["a"], []) is None

+++ practice | Debug: recursion that forgets
--- task
`Tiny` interprets functions whose bodies are expressions: `("num", n)`, `("var", name)`, `("add", a, b)`, `("sub", a, b)`, `("lt", a, b)`, `("if", c, a, b)` and `("call", name, [args])`. Functions are defined with `define(name, params, body)` and called with `call(name, args)`.

The Fibonacci function below should give `fib(10) == 55`, but it gives a wrong answer: the recursive calls overwrite each other's `n`. Find the bug and fix it, so that every call has its own variables.

```python fragment
t = Tiny()
t.define("fib", ["n"], ("if", ("lt", ("var", "n"), ("num", 2)), ("var", "n"), ("add", ("call", "fib", [("sub", ("var", "n"), ("num", 1))]), ("call", "fib", [("sub", ("var", "n"), ("num", 2))]))))
t.call("fib", [10])
```
--- starter
class Tiny:
    def __init__(self):
        self.functions = {}

    def define(self, name, params, body):
        self.functions[name] = (params, body, {})

    def call(self, name, args):
        params, body, env = self.functions[name]
        for p, a in zip(params, args):
            env[p] = a
        return self.ev(body, env)

    def ev(self, e, env):
        kind = e[0]
        if kind == "num":
            return e[1]
        if kind == "var":
            return env[e[1]]
        if kind == "if":
            return self.ev(e[2], env) if self.ev(e[1], env) else self.ev(e[3], env)
        if kind == "call":
            return self.call(e[1], [self.ev(a, env) for a in e[2]])
        a, b = self.ev(e[1], env), self.ev(e[2], env)
        return a + b if kind == "add" else a - b if kind == "sub" else a < b
--- solution
class Tiny:
    def __init__(self):
        self.functions = {}

    def define(self, name, params, body):
        self.functions[name] = (params, body)

    def call(self, name, args):
        params, body = self.functions[name]
        env = dict(zip(params, args))
        return self.ev(body, env)

    def ev(self, e, env):
        kind = e[0]
        if kind == "num":
            return e[1]
        if kind == "var":
            return env[e[1]]
        if kind == "if":
            return self.ev(e[2], env) if self.ev(e[1], env) else self.ev(e[3], env)
        if kind == "call":
            return self.call(e[1], [self.ev(a, env) for a in e[2]])
        a, b = self.ev(e[1], env), self.ev(e[2], env)
        return a + b if kind == "add" else a - b if kind == "sub" else a < b
--- hint
How many dictionaries of variables exist while `fib(10)` runs? How many should there be?
--- hint
Each call needs a new environment of its own, made when the call starts.
