        """Returns (tokens, errors): every token ending with EOF, and every LexError."""
        while self.pos < len(self.source):
            self.scan_token()
        self.tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", self.line, self.col))
        return self.tokens, self.errors

    def scan_token(self):
        line, col = self.line, self.col
        ch = self.peek()
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            self.advance()
        elif ch == "#":
            while self.peek() not in ("", "\n"):
                self.advance()
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            self.number(line, col)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            self.word(line, col)
        elif ch == '"':
            self.string(line, col)
        elif ch + self.peek(1) in TWO_CHAR:
            text = self.advance() + self.advance()
            self.tokens.append(Token("OP", text, line, col))
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            self.tokens.append(Token("OP", self.advance(), line, col))
        else:
            self.advance()   # skip it, report it, and carry on
            message = f"unexpected character {ch!r}"
            if ch in LEX_HINTS:
                message += f" ({LEX_HINTS[ch]})"
            self.errors.append(LexError(message, line, col))

    def number(self, line, col):
        start = self.pos
        while self.peek() in DIGITS:
            self.advance()
        self.tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", self.source[start:self.pos], line, col))

    def word(self, line, col):
        start = self.pos
        while self.peek() in LETTERS or self.peek() in DIGITS:
            self.advance()
        text = self.source[start:self.pos]
        kind = "KEYWORD" if text in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
        self.tokens.append(Token(kind, text, line, col))

    def string(self, line, col):
        """A string literal. The token's text is the decoded value."""
        self.advance()  # the opening quote
        chars = []
        while True:
            ch = self.peek()
            if ch in ("", "\n"):
                # Strings never span lines, so the rest of this line is lost.
                self.errors.append(LexError("unterminated string", line, col))
                return
            if ch == '"':
                self.advance()
                break
            if ch == "\\":
                at_line, at_col = self.line, self.col
                self.advance()
                code = self.peek()
                if code in ESCAPES:
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[self.advance()])
                elif code not in ("", "\n"):
                    self.advance()
                    self.errors.append(LexError(f"unknown escape \\{code}", at_line, at_col))
                continue
            chars.append(self.advance())
        self.tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), line, col))


def tokenize(source):
    """The tokens of source; raises the first LexError if there is one."""
    tokens, errors = Lexer(source).scan()
    if errors:
        raise errors[0]
    return tokens


def point_at(source, line, col):
    """Two lines: source line `line`, and a caret under column `col`.
    Tabs before the column are copied, so the caret lines up in a terminal."""
    lines = source.split("\n")
    text = lines[line - 1] if 1 <= line <= len(lines) else ""
    pad = "".join("\t" if c == "\t" else " " for c in text[:col - 1])
    return text + "\n" + pad.ljust(col - 1) + "^"


# ============================================================================
# The syntax tree
# ============================================================================

def pos_field():
    """A node's line or column: given by keyword, and never part of ==."""
    return field(default=0, kw_only=True, compare=False, repr=False)


@dataclass
class Node:
    line: int = pos_field()
    col: int = pos_field()


@dataclass
class Num(Node):
    value: int


@dataclass
class Str(Node):
    value: str


@dataclass
class Bool(Node):
    value: bool


@dataclass
class Nil(Node):
    pass


@dataclass
class Var(Node):
    name: str
    # How many scopes out the declaration is, or None for a global.
    # Filled in by the resolver.
    depth: object = field(default=None, kw_only=True, compare=False, repr=False)


@dataclass
class Unary(Node):
    op: str
    expr: Node


@dataclass
class Binary(Node):
    op: str
    left: Node
    right: Node


@dataclass
class Call(Node):
    callee: Node
    args: list


@dataclass
class Index(Node):
    target: Node
    index: Node


@dataclass
class ListLit(Node):
    items: list


@dataclass
class MapLit(Node):
    pairs: list     # (key, value) pairs of expressions


@dataclass
class FnExpr(Node):
    params: list    # (name, type) pairs; type is None without an annotation
    ret: object
    body: object    # a Block


@dataclass
class Let(Node):
    name: str
    type: object
    expr: Node


@dataclass
class Assign(Node):
    name: str
    expr: Node
    depth: object = field(default=None, kw_only=True, compare=False, repr=False)


@dataclass
class SetIndex(Node):
    target: Node
    index: Node
    expr: Node


@dataclass
class Print(Node):
    expr: Node


@dataclass
class If(Node):
    cond: Node
    then: object
    else_: object   # None, a Block, or an If (for "else if")


@dataclass
class While(Node):
    cond: Node
    body: object


@dataclass
class For(Node):
    name: str
    iterable: Node
    body: object


@dataclass
class Break(Node):
    pass


@dataclass
class Continue(Node):
    pass


@dataclass
class Fn(Node):
    name: str
    params: list
    ret: object
    body: object


@dataclass
class Return(Node):
    expr: object    # None for a bare "return;"


@dataclass
class ExprStmt(Node):
    expr: Node


@dataclass
class Block(Node):
    stmts: list


@dataclass
class Program(Node):
    stmts: list


# ============================================================================
# The parser
# ============================================================================

class ParseError(StaticError):
    """Tokens in an order the grammar does not allow."""


def describe(tok):
    """How a token is named in an error message."""
    if tok.kind == "EOF":
        return "end of input"
    if tok.kind == "STRING":
        return "a string"
    return f"'{tok.text}'"


# Binding powers, weakest first. An operator with a higher power takes its
# operands before an operator with a lower power does.
LOWEST, OR, AND, NOT, COMPARE, SUM, PRODUCT, UNARY, POSTFIX = range(9)
COMPARISONS = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
INFIX = {
    "or": OR, "and": AND,
    "==": COMPARE, "!=": COMPARE, "<": COMPARE, "<=": COMPARE, ">": COMPARE, ">=": COMPARE,
    "+": SUM, "-": SUM,
    "*": PRODUCT, "/": PRODUCT, "%": PRODUCT,
    "(": POSTFIX, "[": POSTFIX,
}
STATEMENT_START = ("let", "fn", "if", "while", "for", "return", "print", "break", "continue")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str", "list", "map", "any")


class Parser:
    """A Pratt parser for expressions, and recursive descent for statements."""

    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0
        self.errors = []      # every ParseError found so far

    def peek(self):
        return self.tokens[self.pos]

    def at(self, *texts):
        """Is the next token one of these operators or keywords?"""
        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        """Consumes the next token and returns it. EOF is never consumed."""
        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message, tok=None):
        tok = tok or self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}', found {describe(self.peek())}")
        return self.advance()

    # ---- expressions: the Pratt loop -------------------------------------

    def expression(self, power=LOWEST):
        """An expression whose operators all bind more tightly than `power`."""
        left = self.prefix()
        while True:
            tok = self.peek()
            op_power = INFIX.get(tok.text, LOWEST) if tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") else LOWEST
            if op_power <= power:
                return left
            left = self.infix(left, op_power)

    def prefix(self):
        """Something that can start an expression."""
        tok = self.peek()
        where = dict(line=tok.line, col=tok.col)
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text), **where)
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text, **where)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text, **where)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true", **where)
        if self.at("nil"):
            self.advance()
            return Nil(**where)
        if self.at("-", "not"):
            self.advance()
            operand = self.expression(UNARY if tok.text == "-" else NOT)
            return Unary(tok.text, operand, **where)
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expression()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        if self.at("["):
            self.advance()
            return ListLit(self.items("]"), **where)
        if self.at("{"):
            self.advance()
            return MapLit(self.pairs(), **where)
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.function_expr()
        raise self.error(f"expected an expression, found {describe(tok)}")

    def infix(self, left, power):
        """An operator after a complete left operand, and what it needs after it."""
        tok = self.advance()
        where = dict(line=tok.line, col=tok.col)
        if tok.text == "(":
            return Call(left, self.items(")"), line=left.line, col=left.col)
        if tok.text == "[":
            index = self.expression()
            self.expect("]")
            return Index(left, index, **where)
        # A binary operator. The right side may only hold operators that bind
        # more tightly, so a second operator of the same power ends it: that
        # is what makes 10 - 3 - 2 group as (10 - 3) - 2.
        node = Binary(tok.text, left, self.expression(power), **where)
        if tok.text in COMPARISONS and self.at(*COMPARISONS):
            raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return node

    def items(self, close):
        """Comma-separated expressions up to `close`, which is consumed."""
        items = []
        if not self.at(close):
            items.append(self.expression())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                items.append(self.expression())
        self.expect(close)
        return items

    def pairs(self):
        """The key: value pairs of a map literal, up to and including '}'."""
        pairs = []
        if not self.at("}"):
            pairs.append(self.pair())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                pairs.append(self.pair())
        self.expect("}")
        return pairs

    def pair(self):
        key = self.expression()
        self.expect(":")
        return (key, self.expression())

    # ---- statements, with error recovery ---------------------------------

    def program(self):
        """Every statement up to EOF. Errors are collected in self.errors and
        parsing goes on after each one, so one pass reports them all."""
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmt = self.declaration()
            if stmt is not None:
                stmts.append(stmt)
        return Program(stmts)

    def declaration(self):
        """One statement. After a syntax error it records the error, skips to
        a safe place, and returns None."""
        start = self.pos
        try:
            return self.statement()
        except ParseError as e:
            self.errors.append(e)
            self.synchronize(start)
            return None

    def synchronize(self, start):
        """Panic mode: skip to just after a ';', or to a token that starts a
        statement, or to a '}' (so the block around us can close). A block
        entered while skipping is skipped whole, up to its own '}'. Always
        moves at least one token, so parsing cannot get stuck."""
        depth = 0
        if self.pos == start:
            depth = self.skip(depth)
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            if depth == 0:
                before = self.tokens[self.pos - 1]
                if before.kind == "OP" and before.text == ";":
                    return
                if self.at(*STATEMENT_START) or self.at("}"):
                    return
            depth = self.skip(depth)

    def skip(self, depth):
        """Consumes one token while recovering; returns the new block depth."""
        tok = self.advance()
        if tok.kind == "OP" and tok.text == "{":
            return depth + 1
        if tok.kind == "OP" and tok.text == "}" and depth > 0:
            return depth - 1
        return depth

    def statement(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "KEYWORD":
            if tok.text == "fn" and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "IDENT":
                return self.fn_decl()
            handler = {
                "let": self.let_stmt, "print": self.print_stmt, "if": self.if_stmt,
                "while": self.while_stmt, "for": self.for_stmt, "return": self.return_stmt,
                "break": self.jump_stmt, "continue": self.jump_stmt,
            }.get(tok.text)
            if handler is not None:
                return handler()
        return self.simple_stmt()

    def end_statement(self):
        self.expect(";")

    def name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error(f"expected a name, found {describe(tok)}")
        return self.advance()

    def annotation(self, marker):
        """An optional type after ':' or '->'. Nothing checks types yet; they
        are notes for the reader."""
        if not self.at(marker):
            return None
        self.advance()
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error(f"expected a type, found {describe(tok)}")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = self.annotation(":")
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expression()
        self.end_statement()
        return Let(name.text, type_, value, line=name.line, col=name.col)

    def print_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        value = self.expression()
        self.end_statement()
        return Print(value, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def if_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        cond = self.expression()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def while_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        cond = self.expression()
        return While(cond, self.block(), line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def for_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("in")
        iterable = self.expression()
        return For(name.text, iterable, self.block(), line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def return_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        value = None if self.at(";") else self.expression()
        self.end_statement()
        return Return(value, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def jump_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        self.end_statement()
        kind = Break if tok.text == "break" else Continue
        return kind(line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def fn_decl(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        params, ret, body = self.function_rest()
        return Fn(name.text, params, ret, body, line=name.line, col=name.col)

    def function_expr(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        params, ret, body = self.function_rest()
        return FnExpr(params, ret, body, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def function_rest(self):
        """What follows 'fn' or 'fn name': parameters, return type, body."""
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = self.annotation("->")
        return params, ret, self.block()

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        return (name.text, self.annotation(":"))

    def block(self):
        tok = self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error(f"expected '}}' to close the block opened at {tok.line}:{tok.col}, "
                                 f"found end of input")
            stmt = self.declaration()
            if stmt is not None:
                stmts.append(stmt)
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def simple_stmt(self):
        """An assignment (to a name or an index) or an expression statement."""
        expr = self.expression()
        if self.at("="):
            eq = self.advance()
            value = self.expression()
            self.end_statement()
            if isinstance(expr, Var):
                return Assign(expr.name, value, line=expr.line, col=expr.col)
            if isinstance(expr, Index):
                return SetIndex(expr.target, expr.index, value, line=expr.line, col=expr.col)
            # The statement itself was well formed, so report without panicking.
            self.errors.append(self.error("can only assign to a name or an index", eq))
            return None
        self.end_statement()
        return ExprStmt(expr, line=expr.line, col=expr.col)


def parse_expression(source):
    """One expression and nothing after it. Raises the first LexError or ParseError."""
    parser = Parser(tokenize(source))
    expr = parser.expression()
    if parser.peek().kind != "EOF":
        raise parser.error(f"expected end of input, found {describe(parser.peek())}")
    return expr


def parse(source):
    """(program, errors). If the lexer found mistakes, errors are the lexer's
    and program is None: parsing broken tokens only adds confusing errors.
    Otherwise errors are the parser's, and the program must not run unless
    there are none."""
    tokens, errors = Lexer(source).scan()
    if errors:
        return None, errors
    parser = Parser(tokens)
    program = parser.program()
    return program, parser.errors


def quote(text):
    """A string as Comet source writes it: in quotes, with its escapes."""
    return '"' + text.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n") + '"'


def group(head, *parts):
    return "(" + " ".join([head, *parts]) + ")"


def sexpr(node):
    """The tree as a prefix expression, for tests and debugging:
    1 + 2 * x becomes (+ 1 (* 2 x))."""
    if isinstance(node, Num):
        return str(node.value)
    if isinstance(node, Str):
        return quote(node.value)
    if isinstance(node, Bool):
        return "true" if node.value else "false"
    if isinstance(node, Nil):
        return "nil"
    if isinstance(node, Var):
        return node.name
    if isinstance(node, Unary):
        return group(node.op, sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, Binary):
        return group(node.op, sexpr(node.left), sexpr(node.right))
    if isinstance(node, Call):
        return group("call", sexpr(node.callee), *map(sexpr, node.args))
    if isinstance(node, Index):
        return group("index", sexpr(node.target), sexpr(node.index))
    if isinstance(node, ListLit):
        return group("list", *map(sexpr, node.items))
    if isinstance(node, MapLit):
        return group("map", *[sexpr(part) for pair in node.pairs for part in pair])
    return sexpr_statement(node)


def sexpr_statement(node):
    """sexpr for statements and functions: (let x 1), (block ...), ..."""
    if isinstance(node, (Fn, FnExpr)):
        params = "(" + " ".join(name for name, _type in node.params) + ")"
        head = ["fn", node.name] if isinstance(node, Fn) else ["fn"]
        return group(*head, params, sexpr(node.body))
    if isinstance(node, Let):
        return group("let", node.name, sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, Assign):
        return group("set", node.name, sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, SetIndex):
        return group("set", group("index", sexpr(node.target), sexpr(node.index)), sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, Print):
        return group("print", sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, ExprStmt):
        return group("expr", sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, If):
        parts = [sexpr(node.cond), sexpr(node.then)]
        if node.else_ is not None:
            parts.append(sexpr(node.else_))
        return group("if", *parts)
    if isinstance(node, While):
        return group("while", sexpr(node.cond), sexpr(node.body))
    if isinstance(node, For):
        return group("for", node.name, sexpr(node.iterable), sexpr(node.body))
    if isinstance(node, Break):
        return "(break)"
    if isinstance(node, Continue):
        return "(continue)"
    if isinstance(node, Return):
        return "(return)" if node.expr is None else group("return", sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, Block):
        return group("block", *map(sexpr, node.stmts))
    if isinstance(node, Program):
        return group("program", *map(sexpr, node.stmts))
    raise TypeError(f"sexpr cannot show {type(node).__name__}")


# ============================================================================
# The resolver: names and jumps, checked before anything runs
# ============================================================================

class ResolveError(StaticError):
    """A name or a jump used where it cannot be."""


class Resolver:
    """Checks names and jumps before the program runs, and records on each
    Var and Assign how many scopes out the declaration is (None: a global).

    It walks the tree exactly the way the interpreter will, opening a scope
    wherever the interpreter makes an Environment: for a block, for a call
    (the parameters and the body share one), and for each pass of a for loop
    (the loop variable and the body share one)."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.scopes = []      # innermost last; name -> ready (False while its initializer runs)
        self.errors = []
        self.functions = 0    # how many fns we are inside
        self.loops = 0        # how many loops we are inside, within the innermost fn

    def resolve(self, node):
        getattr(self, "visit_" + type(node).__name__)(node)

    def resolve_all(self, nodes):
        for node in nodes:
            self.resolve(node)

    def error(self, message, node):
        self.errors.append(ResolveError(message, node.line, node.col))

    def declare(self, name, node):
        if not self.scopes:
            return   # a global: declaring it again replaces it, which a REPL needs
        scope = self.scopes[-1]
        if name in scope:
            self.error(f"{name} is already declared in this scope", node)
        scope[name] = False

    def define(self, name):
        if self.scopes:
            self.scopes[-1][name] = True

    def resolve_local(self, node, name):
        """Records how many scopes out `name` lives; None if in none of them."""
        for i in range(len(self.scopes) - 1, -1, -1):
            if name in self.scopes[i]:
                node.depth = len(self.scopes) - 1 - i
                return
        node.depth = None   # looked up in the globals when it runs

    def function(self, node):
        outer_loops = self.loops
        self.functions += 1
        self.loops = 0        # a break inside a fn cannot leave a loop outside it
        scope = {}
        for name, _type in node.params:
            if name in scope:
                self.error(f"duplicate parameter {name}", node)
            scope[name] = True
        self.scopes.append(scope)
        self.resolve_all(node.body.stmts)
        self.scopes.pop()
        self.functions -= 1
        self.loops = outer_loops

    # ---- statements ----

    def visit_Program(self, node):
        self.resolve_all(node.stmts)

    def visit_Block(self, node):
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.resolve_all(node.stmts)
        self.scopes.pop()

    def visit_Let(self, node):
        self.declare(node.name, node)
        self.resolve(node.expr)
        self.define(node.name)

    def visit_Assign(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.expr)
        self.resolve_local(node, node.name)

    def visit_SetIndex(self, node):
        self.resolve_all([node.target, node.index, node.expr])

    def visit_Print(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.expr)

    visit_ExprStmt = visit_Print

    def visit_If(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.cond)
        self.resolve(node.then)
        if node.else_ is not None:
            self.resolve(node.else_)

    def visit_While(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.cond)
        self.loops += 1
        self.resolve(node.body)
        self.loops -= 1

    def visit_For(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.iterable)
        self.loops += 1
        self.scopes.append({node.name: True})
        self.resolve_all(node.body.stmts)
        self.scopes.pop()
        self.loops -= 1

    def visit_Break(self, node):
        if self.loops == 0:
            self.error("break outside a loop", node)

    def visit_Continue(self, node):
        if self.loops == 0:
            self.error("continue outside a loop", node)

    def visit_Return(self, node):
        if self.functions == 0:
            self.error("return outside a function", node)
        if node.expr is not None:
            self.resolve(node.expr)

    def visit_Fn(self, node):
        self.declare(node.name, node)
        self.define(node.name)    # before the body, so the fn can call itself
        self.function(node)

    # ---- expressions ----

    def visit_FnExpr(self, node):
        self.function(node)

    def visit_Var(self, node):
        if self.scopes and self.scopes[-1].get(node.name) is False:
            self.error(f"cannot read {node.name} in its own initializer", node)
        self.resolve_local(node, node.name)

    def visit_Num(self, node):
        pass

    visit_Str = visit_Bool = visit_Nil = visit_Num

    def visit_Unary(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.expr)

    def visit_Binary(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.left)
        self.resolve(node.right)

    def visit_Call(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.callee)
        self.resolve_all(node.args)

    def visit_Index(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.target)
        self.resolve(node.index)

    def visit_ListLit(self, node):
        self.resolve_all(node.items)

    def visit_MapLit(self, node):
        for key, value in node.pairs:
            self.resolve(key)
            self.resolve(value)


def resolve(program):
    """Resolves every name in program; returns the list of ResolveErrors."""
    resolver = Resolver()
    resolver.resolve(program)
    return resolver.errors


# ============================================================================
# Values
# ============================================================================

class CometError(Exception):
    """A runtime error in the Comet program (not a bug in the interpreter)."""


def comet_div(a, b):
    """Integer division that rounds toward zero, like C."""
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def type_name(value):
    """Comet's name for a value's type."""
    if value is None:
        return "nil"
    if isinstance(value, bool):     # before int: in Python, True is an int
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return "str"
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return "list"
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return "map"
    if isinstance(value, (Closure, Builtin)):
        return "fn"
    raise TypeError(f"not a Comet value: {value!r}")


def repr_value(value):
    """A value as Comet source writes it: strings in quotes."""
    if value is None:
        return "nil"
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return str(value)
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return quote(value)
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return "[" + ", ".join(repr_value(item) for item in value) + "]"
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return "{" + ", ".join(f"{quote(k)}: {repr_value(v)}" for k, v in value.items()) + "}"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return f"<fn {value.name}>" if value.name else "<fn>"
    if isinstance(value, Builtin):
        return f"<builtin {value.name}>"
    raise TypeError(f"not a Comet value: {value!r}")


def show(value):
    """What print writes: a string as it is, anything else as repr_value."""
    return value if isinstance(value, str) else repr_value(value)


def values_equal(a, b):
    """Comet's ==: values of different types are never equal."""
    if type_name(a) != type_name(b):
        return False
    if isinstance(a, list):
        return len(a) == len(b) and all(values_equal(x, y) for x, y in zip(a, b))
    if isinstance(a, dict):
        return a.keys() == b.keys() and all(values_equal(a[k], b[k]) for k in a)
    return a == b    # same Comet type, so Python's == is right (fns: the same fn)


ARITHMETIC = {
    "+": operator.add, "-": operator.sub, "*": operator.mul, "/": comet_div, "%": comet_mod,
    "<": operator.lt, "<=": operator.le, ">": operator.gt, ">=": operator.ge,
}
ORDERING = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=")
JOINABLE = ("str", "list")      # + also joins two of these (a new value)


def arithmetic(op, left, right):
    """+ - * / % < <= > >= with Comet's type rules."""
    lt, rt = type_name(left), type_name(right)
    if lt == rt == "int":
        return ARITHMETIC[op](left, right)
    if op == "+" and lt == rt and lt in JOINABLE:
        return left + right
    if op in ORDERING and lt == rt == "str":
        return ARITHMETIC[op](left, right)
    raise CometError(f"'{op}' cannot combine {lt} and {rt}")


class Closure:
    """A Comet function value: its declaration (an Fn or FnExpr node) and
    the Environment it was made in, which it keeps alive."""

    def __init__(self, decl, env):
        self.decl = decl
        self.env = env

    @property
    def name(self):
        return self.decl.name if isinstance(self.decl, Fn) else None

    def label(self):
        return self.name or "anonymous fn"


class ReturnSignal(Exception):
    """Carries a return value up to the call waiting for it. Not a
    CometError, so nothing a Comet program does can catch it."""

    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value


def check_arity(name, fewest, most, got):
    if fewest <= got <= most:
        return
    if fewest == most:
        wanted = f"{fewest} argument" + ("" if fewest == 1 else "s")
    elif most == fewest + 1:
        wanted = f"{fewest} or {most} arguments"
    else:
        wanted = f"{fewest} to {most} arguments"
    raise CometError(f"{name} expects {wanted}, got {got}")


class Builtin:
    """A function written in Python. It gets the interpreter first, then the
    Comet arguments."""

    def __init__(self, name, fn, arity):
        self.name = name
        self.fn = fn
        self.fewest, self.most = (arity, arity) if isinstance(arity, int) else arity

    def label(self):
        return self.name


class BreakSignal(Exception):
    """Thrown by break; caught by the innermost loop."""


class ContinueSignal(Exception):
    """Thrown by continue; caught by the innermost loop, which goes on."""
SEQUENCES = ("list", "str")
SIZED = ("list", "str", "map")


def checked_index(seq, index):
    """index, after checking it is an int inside seq; else CometError."""
    if type_name(index) != "int":
        raise CometError(f"an index must be int, not {type_name(index)}")
    if not 0 <= index < len(seq):
        raise CometError(f"index {index} out of range for a {type_name(seq)} of length {len(seq)}")
    return index


def map_key(key):
    if type_name(key) != "str":
        raise CometError(f"map keys must be str, not {type_name(key)}")
    return key


def get_item(target, index):
    """target[index], with Comet's checks."""
    kind = type_name(target)
    if kind == "map":
        key = map_key(index)
        if key not in target:
            raise CometError(f"no key {quote(key)} in map")
        return target[key]
    if kind in SEQUENCES:
        return target[checked_index(target, index)]
    raise CometError(f"cannot index a value of type {kind}")


def set_item(target, index, value):
    """target[index] = value, with Comet's checks."""
    kind = type_name(target)
    if kind == "list":
        target[checked_index(target, index)] = value
    elif kind == "map":
        target[map_key(index)] = value
    elif kind == "str":
        raise CometError("strings cannot be changed; build a new one instead")
    else:
        raise CometError(f"cannot index a value of type {kind}")


def iteration(value):
    """The items a for loop walks through, as a list made before the loop
    starts: a body that changes the value cannot confuse the loop."""
    kind = type_name(value)
    if kind == "list":
        return list(value)
    if kind == "str":
        return list(value)          # one-character strings
    if kind == "map":
        return list(value.keys())   # the keys, in the order they were added
    raise CometError(f"cannot loop over a value of type {kind}")


# ============================================================================
# The standard library
# ============================================================================

BUILTINS = {}   # name -> (Python function, arity); every Interpreter defines them


def builtin(name, arity):
    """Registers the decorated Python function as a Comet builtin. arity is a
    number, or a (fewest, most) pair."""
    def register(fn):
        BUILTINS[name] = (fn, arity)
        return fn
    return register


def expect_type(name, value, *kinds):
    """Raises CometError unless value's type is one of kinds."""
    if type_name(value) not in kinds:
        wanted = kinds[0] if len(kinds) == 1 else ", ".join(kinds[:-1]) + " or " + kinds[-1]
        raise CometError(f"{name} needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")


@builtin("len", 1)
def builtin_len(interp, value):
    expect_type("len", value, *SIZED)
    return len(value)


@builtin("push", 2)
def builtin_push(interp, items, value):
    expect_type("push", items, "list")
    items.append(value)     # in place: every name for this list sees it
    return None


@builtin("items", 1)
def builtin_items(interp, table):
    """The map's [key, value] pairs, in the order the keys were added."""
    expect_type("items", table, "map")
    return [[key, value] for key, value in table.items()]


@builtin("ord", 1)
def builtin_ord(interp, char):
    expect_type("ord", char, "str")
    if len(char) != 1:
        raise CometError(f"ord needs a string of one character, not {len(char)}")
    return ord(char)


@builtin("chr", 1)
def builtin_chr(interp, code):
    expect_type("chr", code, "int")
    if not 0 <= code <= 0x10FFFF:
        raise CometError(f"chr needs a code from 0 to 1114111, not {code}")
    return chr(code)


@builtin("keys", 1)
def builtin_keys(interp, table):
    expect_type("keys", table, "map")
    return list(table)


@builtin("values", 1)
def builtin_values(interp, table):
    expect_type("values", table, "map")
    return list(table.values())


@builtin("has", 2)
def builtin_has(interp, table, key):
    expect_type("has", table, "map")
    return map_key(key) in table


@builtin("remove", 2)
def builtin_remove(interp, table, key):
    expect_type("remove", table, "map")
    key = map_key(key)
    if key not in table:
        raise CometError(f"no key {quote(key)} in map")
    return table.pop(key)


# ============================================================================
# The interpreter
# ============================================================================


class Environment:
    """One scope's variables, and the scope around it (None for the globals)."""

    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        if self.parent is not None and name in self.values:
            raise CometError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.values[name] = value

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env.values[name]
            env = env.parent
        raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                env.values[name] = value
                return
            env = env.parent
        raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {name}")

    def ancestor(self, depth):
        """The scope `depth` steps out from this one."""
        env = self
        for _ in range(depth):
            env = env.parent
        return env


class Interpreter:
    """Runs a syntax tree. Printed lines collect in self.output."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.env = self.globals       # the scope running now
        self.output = []
        for name, (fn, arity) in BUILTINS.items():
            self.globals.define(name, Builtin(name, fn, arity))

    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def handler(self, prefix, node):
        """The method for this kind of node: exec_Print for a Print, and so on."""
        method = getattr(self, prefix + type(node).__name__, None)
        if method is None:
            raise CometError(f"{type(node).__name__} is not supported yet")
        return method

    def execute(self, stmt):
        self.handler("exec_", stmt)(stmt)

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        return self.handler("eval_", expr)(expr)

    def execute_block(self, stmts, env):
        """Runs stmts with env as the current scope, and always puts the old
        scope back, also when a statement raises."""
        previous = self.env
        self.env = env
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.execute(stmt)
        finally:
            self.env = previous

    # ---- statements ----

    def exec_Let(self, stmt):
        self.env.define(stmt.name, self.evaluate(stmt.expr))

    def exec_Assign(self, stmt):
        value = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        if stmt.depth is None:
            self.globals.assign(stmt.name, value)
        else:
            self.env.ancestor(stmt.depth).values[stmt.name] = value

    def exec_Print(self, stmt):
        self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))

    def exec_ExprStmt(self, stmt):
        self.evaluate(stmt.expr)

    def exec_If(self, stmt):
        if self.condition(stmt.cond):
            self.execute(stmt.then)
        elif stmt.else_ is not None:
            self.execute(stmt.else_)    # a Block, or an If for "else if"

    def exec_While(self, stmt):
        while self.condition(stmt.cond):
            try:
                self.execute(stmt.body)
            except BreakSignal:
                break
            except ContinueSignal:
                pass

    def exec_Block(self, stmt):
        self.execute_block(stmt.stmts, Environment(self.env))

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"a condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    # ---- expressions ----

    def eval_Num(self, expr):
        return expr.value

    eval_Str = eval_Bool = eval_Num

    def eval_Nil(self, expr):
        return None

    def eval_Var(self, expr):
        if expr.depth is None:
            return self.globals.lookup(expr.name)
        return self.env.ancestor(expr.depth).values[expr.name]

    def eval_Unary(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
        if expr.op == "-":
            self.need("int", value, "-")
            return -value
        self.need("bool", value, "not")
        return not value

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def eval_Binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if left == (op == "or"):     # false and ..., true or ...: already decided
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            lt, rt = type_name(left), type_name(right)
            if lt != rt and "nil" not in (lt, rt):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {lt} with {rt}")
            return values_equal(left, right) == (op == "==")
        return arithmetic(op, left, right)

    # ---- functions ----

    def exec_Fn(self, stmt):
        self.env.define(stmt.name, Closure(stmt, self.env))

    def eval_FnExpr(self, expr):
        return Closure(expr, self.env)

    def exec_Return(self, stmt):
        value = None if stmt.expr is None else self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        raise ReturnSignal(value)

    def eval_Call(self, expr):
        callee = self.evaluate(expr.callee)
        args = [self.evaluate(arg) for arg in expr.args]
        return self.call(callee, args)

    def call(self, callee, args):
        """Calls a function value with argument values, and returns its result."""
        if isinstance(callee, Closure):
            params = callee.decl.params
            check_arity(callee.label(), len(params), len(params), len(args))
            env = Environment(callee.env)   # inside the fn's own scope, not the caller's
            for (name, _type), value in zip(params, args):
                env.define(name, value)
            try:
                self.execute_block(callee.decl.body.stmts, env)
            except ReturnSignal as signal:
                return signal.value
            return None
        if isinstance(callee, Builtin):
            check_arity(callee.name, callee.fewest, callee.most, len(args))
            return callee.fn(self, *args)
        raise CometError(f"cannot call a value of type {type_name(callee)}")

    # ---- lists, loops and jumps ----

    def eval_ListLit(self, expr):
        return [self.evaluate(item) for item in expr.items]

    def eval_Index(self, expr):
        target = self.evaluate(expr.target)
        return get_item(target, self.evaluate(expr.index))

    def exec_SetIndex(self, stmt):
        target = self.evaluate(stmt.target)
        index = self.evaluate(stmt.index)
        set_item(target, index, self.evaluate(stmt.expr))

    def exec_For(self, stmt):
        for item in iteration(self.evaluate(stmt.iterable)):
            env = Environment(self.env)     # a fresh variable for every pass
            env.define(stmt.name, item)
            try:
                self.execute_block(stmt.body.stmts, env)
            except BreakSignal:
                break
            except ContinueSignal:
                pass

    def exec_Break(self, stmt):
        raise BreakSignal()

    def exec_Continue(self, stmt):
        raise ContinueSignal()

    def eval_MapLit(self, expr):
        table = {}
        for key, value in expr.pairs:
            table[map_key(self.evaluate(key))] = self.evaluate(value)
        return table


def run(source):
    """Runs a Comet program and returns what it printed, one line per print.
    Errors found before running are the whole answer; a runtime error is
    added after whatever was printed before it."""
    program, errors = parse(source)
    if not errors:
        errors = resolve(program)
    if errors:
        return "\n".join(str(e) for e in errors)
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(program)
    except CometError as e:
        interp.output.append(f"runtime error: {e}")
    return "\n".join(interp.output)
--- hint
The value helpers each gain an `isinstance(value, dict)` case. For `repr_value`, build `f"{quote(k)}: {repr_value(v)}"` for each pair. For `values_equal`, compare `a.keys() == b.keys()` first (dict key views compare as sets).
--- hint
`get_item` handles `"map"` before the sequence case: check the key with `map_key`, then raise if it is missing. `set_item` gains two `elif` branches. `iteration` returns `list(value)` for a str and `list(value.keys())` for a map.
--- hint
`eval_MapLit` builds a dict with `table[map_key(self.evaluate(key))] = self.evaluate(value)` for each pair. The four builtins are one short decorated function each; `remove` can use `dict.pop` after checking the key exists.

+++ practice | Writing nested maps and lists
--- task
Write `show(value)` that writes a Python value standing for a Comet value in Comet's source form: `None` as `nil`, bools as `true`/`false`, ints as digits, strings in double quotes (escape `\` as `\\`, `"` as `\"` and a newline as `\n`), lists as `[a, b]` and dicts as `{"key": value, …}` in their insertion order, with `", "` between items and `": "` after each key. Nesting can go to any depth.

For example, `show({"id": 7, "tags": ["a", None], "ok": True})` is `{"id": 7, "tags": ["a", nil], "ok": true}`.
--- starter
def show(value):
    return str(value)
--- solution
def quote(text):
    return '"' + text.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n") + '"'


def show(value):
    if value is None:
        return "nil"
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return str(value)
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return quote(value)
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return "[" + ", ".join(show(item) for item in value) + "]"
    return "{" + ", ".join(f"{quote(k)}: {show(v)}" for k, v in value.items()) + "}"
--- hint
One case per type, and the list and dict cases call `show` on their parts. Test `bool` before `int`.
--- hint
Escape the backslash first when quoting, or the backslashes added for quotes would be doubled.
--- check case | The example
show({"id": 7, "tags": ["a", None], "ok": True})
=> '{"id": 7, "tags": ["a", nil], "ok": true}'
--- check case | Empty containers and deep nesting
(show({}), show([]), show({"a": {"b": [[{}]]}}))
=> ("{}", "[]", '{"a": {"b": [[{}]]}}')
--- check case | Escapes, in keys and in values
show({'say "hi"': "back\\slash\nnew"})
=> '{"say \\"hi\\"": "back\\\\slash\\nnew"}'
--- check case | Insertion order is kept
show({"z": 1, "a": 2, "m": False})
=> '{"z": 1, "a": 2, "m": false}'

+++ practice | Reading a string literal
--- task
Write `unquote(text)`, the reverse of quoting: `text` is a Comet string literal, such as `"a\"b"` (the quotes are part of the text), and the function returns the string it stands for. The escapes are `\"`, `\\` and `\n`. Raise `ValueError` with exactly these messages:

- `not a string literal` if `text` does not start and end with a `"` (a lone `"` is not a literal either);
- `unknown escape \X at col N` for a backslash followed by any other character X, where N is the backslash's column (from 1, counting the opening quote as column 1);
- `unescaped quote at col N` for a `"` inside the literal that is not escaped;
- `backslash at the end` if a backslash is the last character before the closing quote.

For example, `unquote('"say \\"hi\\""')` (the text `"say \"hi\""`) is `say "hi"`.
--- starter
def unquote(text):
    return text[1:-1]
--- solution
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}


def unquote(text):
    if len(text) < 2 or text[0] != '"' or text[-1] != '"':
        raise ValueError("not a string literal")
    out = []
    i = 1
    end = len(text) - 1
    while i < end:
        ch = text[i]
        if ch == "\\":
            if i + 1 >= end:
                raise ValueError("backslash at the end")
            code = text[i + 1]
            if code not in ESCAPES:
                raise ValueError(f"unknown escape \\{code} at col {i + 1}")
            out.append(ESCAPES[code])
            i += 2
        elif ch == '"':
            raise ValueError(f"unescaped quote at col {i + 1}")
        else:
            out.append(ch)
            i += 1
    return "".join(out)
--- hint
Check the outer quotes first, then walk the characters between them with an index, so an escape can consume two characters at once.
--- hint
A backslash whose next character is the closing quote is "at the end": the closing quote cannot be escaped, or the literal would never close.
--- check case | The example, and a newline escape
(unquote('"say \\"hi\\""'), unquote('"a\\nb"'), unquote('"back\\\\slash"'))
=> ('say "hi"', "a\nb", "back\\slash")
--- check case | The empty string
unquote('""')
=> ""
--- check test | Not a literal
all(raises(ValueError, lambda t=t: unquote(t)) for t in ['abc', '"abc', 'abc"', '"', ""])
--- check test | Bad escapes and stray quotes name their column
__import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "^unknown escape \\\\t at col 3$", unquote, '"a\\tb"') is None and __import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "^unescaped quote at col 3$", unquote, '"a"b"') is None and __import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "^backslash at the end$", unquote, '"ab\\"') is None

+++ practice | One lookup for lists, strings and maps
--- task
Write `get_value(container, key)` with Comet's rules for Python values: lists and strings take an int position (not a bool) with `0 <= key < len`, and a string gives a one-character string; dicts take a string key that must be present. Raise `LookupError` with exactly these messages:

- `cannot index a value of type T` for anything that is not a list, string or dict (T is `nil`, `bool`, `int`, `str`, `list` or `map`);
- `an index must be int, not T` for a list or string with a bad position type;
- `index I out of range for a T of length N` (T is `list` or `str`);
- `map keys must be str, not T` for a dict with a key that is not a string;
- `no key "K" in map` for a missing key (K as it is, with no escaping).

For example, `get_value("abc", 1)` is `"b"` and `get_value({"a": [1]}, "a")` is `[1]`.
--- starter
def get_value(container, key):
    return container[key]
--- solution
def comet_type(v):
    if v is None:
        return "nil"
    if isinstance(v, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(v, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(v, str):
        return "str"
    if isinstance(v, list):
        return "list"
    return "map"


def get_value(container, key):
    kind = comet_type(container)
    if kind == "map":
        if not isinstance(key, str):
            raise LookupError(f"map keys must be str, not {comet_type(key)}")
        if key not in container:
            raise LookupError(f'no key "{key}" in map')
        return container[key]
    if kind not in ("list", "str"):
        raise LookupError(f"cannot index a value of type {kind}")
    if comet_type(key) != "int":
        raise LookupError(f"an index must be int, not {comet_type(key)}")
    if not 0 <= key < len(container):
        raise LookupError(f"index {key} out of range for a {kind} of length {len(container)}")
    return container[key]
--- hint
Decide by the container's type first: maps check their key one way, lists and strings another, and everything else is an error.
--- hint
A helper that names the Comet type of any value keeps every message to one line.
--- check case | Good lookups
(get_value("abc", 1), get_value({"a": [1]}, "a"), get_value([None, 2], 0), get_value({"": 0}, ""))
=> ("b", [1], None, 0)
--- check test | Positions out of range, for both sequences
__import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(LookupError, "^index 3 out of range for a str of length 3$", get_value, "abc", 3) is None and __import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(LookupError, "^index -1 out of range for a list of length 1$", get_value, [5], -1) is None
--- check test | Bad key types
__import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(LookupError, "^an index must be int, not bool$", get_value, "abc", False) is None and __import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(LookupError, "^map keys must be str, not int$", get_value, {"1": 1}, 1) is None
--- check test | Missing keys and things that cannot be indexed
__import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(LookupError, '^no key "b" in map$', get_value, {"a": 1}, "b") is None and __import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(LookupError, "^cannot index a value of type nil$", get_value, None, 0) is None and __import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(LookupError, "^cannot index a value of type int$", get_value, 5, 0) is None

+++ practice | Map equality, with nesting and strict types
--- task
Write `same(a, b)` for Python values standing for Comet values (`None`, bools, ints, strings, lists and dicts with string keys, nested to any depth). Values are the same when they have the same Comet type, and: lists have the same length and pairwise same items, in order; dicts have the same set of keys and the same value for every key, **in any order**; other values are equal by Python's `==`. A bool is never the same as an int, and a dict is never the same as a list, even when both are empty.

For example, `same({"a": 1, "b": [2]}, {"b": [2], "a": 1})` is `True`.
--- starter
def same(a, b):
    return a == b
--- solution
def comet_type(v):
    if v is None:
        return "nil"
    if isinstance(v, bool):
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(v, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(v, str):
        return "str"
    if isinstance(v, list):
        return "list"
    return "map"


def same(a, b):
    if comet_type(a) != comet_type(b):
        return False
    if isinstance(a, list):
        return len(a) == len(b) and all(same(x, y) for x, y in zip(a, b))
    if isinstance(a, dict):
        return a.keys() == b.keys() and all(same(a[k], b[k]) for k in a)
    return a == b
--- hint
Compare type names first. For dicts, compare the key sets, then the values key by key; for lists, the lengths, then the items in order.
--- hint
`a.keys() == b.keys()` compares keys as sets, so order does not matter, which is exactly what map equality needs.
--- check case | Key order does not matter, list order does
(same({"a": 1, "b": [2]}, {"b": [2], "a": 1}), same([1, 2], [2, 1]), same({"x": [1, 2]}, {"x": [2, 1]}))
=> (True, False, False)
--- check case | Strict types inside maps
(same({"a": 1}, {"a": True}), same({"a": None}, {"a": None}), same({"a": {"b": 0}}, {"a": {"b": False}}))
=> (False, True, False)
--- check case | Different keys, and empty containers of different kinds
(same({"a": 1}, {"a": 1, "b": 2}), same({}, []), same({}, {}), same([], []))
=> (False, False, True, True)

+++ practice | Debug: dropping rare words
--- task
`drop_rare(counts, minimum)` takes a dict of word counts and removes, **in place**, every word whose count is below `minimum`; it returns the sorted list of the words it removed. It crashes with `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration` whenever there is something to remove. Fix it; the caller's dict must be the one that changes.
--- starter
def drop_rare(counts, minimum):
    removed = []
    for word in counts:
        if counts[word] < minimum:
            del counts[word]
            removed.append(word)
    return sorted(removed)
--- solution
def drop_rare(counts, minimum):
    removed = []
    for word in list(counts):
        if counts[word] < minimum:
            del counts[word]
            removed.append(word)
    return sorted(removed)
--- hint
Python does not allow a dict to gain or lose keys while a loop is walking it. What could the loop walk instead?
--- hint
Walk a snapshot of the keys, as Comet's `for` over a map does, and delete from the real dict.
--- check test | Rare words are removed from the same dict
(lambda c: drop_rare(c, 2) == ["or", "red"] and c == {"to": 3, "be": 2})({"to": 3, "or": 1, "be": 2, "red": 1})

+++ practice | Reading Comet values back
--- task
Write `parse_value(text)`, the reverse of writing a value: it reads Comet's literal syntax and returns the Python value.

- `nil`, `true`, `false`; whole numbers with an optional `-` straight in front (`-12`);
- strings in double quotes with the escapes `\"`, `\\` and `\n`;
- lists `[v, v, …]` and maps `{"key": v, …}` with string keys, nested to any depth, possibly empty.

Spaces and newlines may appear between any two parts. Anything else, including trailing text after a complete value, raises `ValueError`. For example, `parse_value('{"a": [1, -2, nil], "b\\n": true}')` is `{"a": [1, -2, None], "b\n": True}`.
--- starter
def parse_value(text):
    return None
--- solution
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
WORDS = {"nil": None, "true": True, "false": False}


def parse_value(text):
    pos = 0

    def skip():
        nonlocal pos
        while pos < len(text) and text[pos] in " \n\t":
            pos += 1

    def expect(ch):
        nonlocal pos
        skip()
        if pos >= len(text) or text[pos] != ch:
            raise ValueError(f"expected {ch!r} at {pos}")
        pos += 1

    def string():
        nonlocal pos
        expect('"')
        out = []
        while True:
            if pos >= len(text) or text[pos] == "\n":
                raise ValueError("unterminated string")
            ch = text[pos]
            if ch == '"':
                pos += 1
                return "".join(out)
            if ch == "\\":
                if pos + 1 >= len(text) or text[pos + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                    raise ValueError("bad escape")
                out.append(ESCAPES[text[pos + 1]])
                pos += 2
            else:
                out.append(ch)
                pos += 1

    def sequence(close, item):
        nonlocal pos
        items = []
        skip()
        if pos < len(text) and text[pos] == close:
            pos += 1
            return items
        while True:
            items.append(item())
            skip()
            if pos < len(text) and text[pos] == ",":
                pos += 1
                continue
            expect(close)
            return items

    def pair():
        key = string()
        expect(":")
        return key, value()

    def value():
        nonlocal pos
        skip()
        if pos >= len(text):
            raise ValueError("unexpected end")
        ch = text[pos]
        if ch == '"':
            return string()
        if ch == "[":
            pos += 1
            return sequence("]", value)
        if ch == "{":
            pos += 1
            return dict(sequence("}", pair))
        for word, result in WORDS.items():
            if text.startswith(word, pos):
                pos += len(word)
                return result
        start = pos
        if ch == "-":
            pos += 1
        digits = pos
        while pos < len(text) and text[pos] in "0123456789":
            pos += 1
        if pos == digits:
            raise ValueError(f"unexpected {ch!r} at {start}")
        return int(text[start:pos])

    result = value()
    skip()
    if pos != len(text):
        raise ValueError(f"trailing text at {pos}")
    return result
--- hint
Write it as a small recursive-descent parser with a position: `value()` looks at the next character and decides what comes: a string, a list, a map, a word, or a number.
--- hint
Lists and maps share one helper: comma-separated items up to a closing bracket, where the item reader is passed in (a value for lists, a `"key": value` pair for maps).
--- check case | The example
parse_value('{"a": [1, -2, nil], "b\\n": true}')
=> {"a": [1, -2, None], "b\n": True}
--- check case | Plain values and empty containers
[parse_value(t) for t in ["nil", "false", "  42 ", "-7", '""', "[]", "{ }", '"q\\"x"']]
=> [None, False, 42, -7, "", [], {}, 'q"x']
--- check case | Deep nesting with spaces and newlines
parse_value('[ {"k" :\n [ [], {"z": "w"} ] } , 3 ]')
=> [{"k": [[], {"z": "w"}]}, 3]
--- check test | Malformed text
all(raises(ValueError, lambda t=t: parse_value(t)) for t in ["", "[1,", "[1 2]", '{"a" 1}', "{1: 2}", "tru", "- 5", '"abc', "1 2", "[1,]", '"\\t"', "{,}"])
--- check test | Round trip with Comet's written form
(lambda v: parse_value('{"id": 7, "tags": ["a", nil], "ok": true, "s": "back\\\\slash"}') == v)({"id": 7, "tags": ["a", None], "ok": True, "s": "back\\slash"})

=== cap-interp-09 | The standard library and functions as values
--- teach
Comet has the data structures now: lists, maps and strings. What it lacks is the everyday toolbox that makes a language pleasant: turning numbers into text and back, sorting, splitting a line into words, and above all the **higher-order functions** `map`, `filter` and `reduce`, which take a Comet function as an argument and call it. This milestone builds that **standard library**, and the interesting part is the last one: a builtin written in Python that calls back into Comet code.

### Builtin or Comet code?

A library function can be written in two ways:

- **natively**, in Python, as a `@builtin`; or
- **in Comet itself**, as ordinary Comet code loaded before the program starts, often called a [[prelude|prelude]].

Native functions are much faster (a Python loop runs perhaps fifty times faster than the same loop interpreted by Comet), and some things, like the length of a list, cannot be written in Comet at all. Comet code is shorter, gets error messages and traces for free, and shows off the language. This milestone writes the whole library natively. Milestone 12 writes a piece in Comet, the test runner, where speed does not matter.

The starter already gives many easy builtins: `type`, `str`, `abs`, `sum`, `min`, `max`, `reverse`, `repeat`, `upper`, `lower`, `trim`, `find`, `starts_with`, `ends_with` and `replace`. Read them: each is a few lines, checks its arguments with `expect_type`, and then uses Python. `string_builtin` even makes three builtins from one Python function by giving each its own name, a closure in Python.

### Conversions

- `str(v)` is what `print` would write: `show(v)`.
- `int(v)` turns a string into an int: spaces around it are allowed, then an optional `-`, then ASCII digits. Anything else fails with `cannot turn "12a" into an int`, and an int comes back unchanged. The check is strict on purpose. Python's `int()` accepts `"1_000"`, `"+5"` and Arabic-Indic digits, and Comet should not inherit rules nobody chose.
- `range(n)` is the list `[0, 1, …, n − 1]`, and `range(a, b)` is `[a, …, b − 1]`. It takes 1 or 2 arguments, the first builtin with a range of arities, which `check_arity` already handles.

### Sorting

`sort(xs)` returns a **new** sorted list and leaves `xs` alone. The items must be all ints or all strings: `sort needs a list of all int or all str`. Python itself would raise `TypeError: '<' not supported between 'int' and 'str'`, and a Python exception escaping from the interpreter is always a bug: the Comet program should see a Comet error. Python's `sorted` is Timsort, a stable O(n log n) merge sort, so Comet's sort is stable too.

### Functions as arguments

Here is the heart of the milestone:

```text
let squares = map([1, 2, 3], fn (x) { return x * x; });
let evens = filter(range(10), fn (n) { return n % 2 == 0; });
let total = reduce([4, 5, 6], fn (sum, x) { return sum + x; }, 0);
```

`map(xs, f)` returns a new list of `f(x)` for each item. `filter(xs, f)` keeps the items for which `f` returns `true`. `reduce(xs, f, start)` folds the list into one value: starting with `start`, it replaces the running value with `f(running, x)` for each item in turn. A function that takes or returns functions is called **higher-order**, and these three are the classic trio from functional programming.

`f` can be any function value: a named function, an anonymous one, a closure, or a builtin, so `map(words, len)` works.

### Calling back into the interpreter

`builtin_map` is Python code, and `f` is a Comet `Closure`. How does Python call it? Through the interpreter: every builtin receives the interpreter as its first argument, and `interp.call(f, [item])` runs the Comet function exactly as a call in Comet source would. `call` already does everything needed: it checks the arity, makes the new environment from the closure's, runs the body, catches the `ReturnSignal`, and handles builtins too.

This is called **re-entrancy** (see the [[re-entrant code note|reentrant]]): the interpreter is in the middle of evaluating a call to `map` when `map` asks it to evaluate more code. It works because of an invariant kept since milestone 4: *every piece of interpreter state that a call changes is put back when the call ends*. `self.env` is restored by `execute_block`'s `finally`. Nothing else is global. So the callback can do anything, including calling `map` itself, and when it returns, the outer evaluation carries on exactly where it was. A callback that raises a `CometError` sends it straight up through `map` to the program, with the environment already restored.

Two more rules make the trio safe:

- Each walks a **snapshot** of the list, as `for` does: a callback that pushes to the list it is being mapped over cannot make `map` run forever.
- `filter`'s function must return a real bool: `filter's function must return bool, not int`. No truthiness, as for `if`.

A value passed where a function is needed is caught with `expect_function`: `map needs a function, not int`.

### Strings, split and joined

- `split(text, sep)` cuts a string at every occurrence of a separator: `split("a,b,,c", ",")` is `["a", "b", "", "c"]`. Empty pieces are kept, so `join(split(s, sep), sep)` always gives back `s`. An empty separator is an error: splitting at "nothing" has no sensible answer.
- `join(xs, sep)` glues a list of strings with the separator between them. Every item must be a string: `join needs a list of str`.
- `slice(v, start, end)` is the part of a string or list from `start` up to, not including, `end`. Positions past the end are cut back to the end, as in Python, so `slice("abc", 1, 99)` is `"bc"`, and `start` beyond `end` gives an empty result. Negative positions are errors, like negative indexes.
- `contains(container, item)` asks whether a string contains a substring, or a list contains a value, compared with `values_equal`, so `contains([1], true)` is `false`.

`join` is the right way to build a long string. Adding strings one piece at a time with `+` copies everything built so far on every step, O(n²) in total; collecting the pieces in a list and joining once is O(n).

### Why it is correct

Each builtin checks its arguments' types before using Python, so it only ever applies a Python operation to values for which Comet's rule and Python's rule agree. That is the whole trick of reusing Python's values safely. The higher-order builtins call Comet functions only through `interp.call`, the same path as a call in the source, so a callback behaves exactly as it would if the program had called it directly: same arity check, same scoping, same return handling.

### What it costs

`map` and `filter` make n calls, each costing whatever the callback costs, plus O(n) for the snapshot and the result. `sort` is O(n log n) comparisons, done by Python at native speed. `split`, `join`, `slice` and `contains` are linear in the lengths involved. A native builtin runs dozens of times faster than the same algorithm written in Comet and interpreted node by node, which is the argument for writing a library natively.

### How to test it

Each builtin with typical arguments, then its edge cases (empty list, empty string, positions past the end), then its type errors and arity errors. For the higher-order ones: a named function, an anonymous one, a closure and a builtin as the callback; a callback that calls `map` itself; a callback that raises an error; a callback that pushes to the list; and `filter` with a non-bool result. Finally a small pipeline that combines several of them.

### Where it is used

- `map`, `filter` and `reduce` go back to Lisp in the 1950s and 60s, and are in Python, JavaScript, Java's streams and every functional language. [[Google's MapReduce|mapreduce]] borrowed the names for computing across thousands of machines.
- Every serious interpreter has a native standard library in its implementation language: CPython's is in C, and Lua's is a set of C functions registered much as `@builtin` registers Python ones.

**Watch out:** library bugs in an interpreter.

- Calling the Python function inside a `Closure` directly, or trying to, instead of going through `interp.call`: the callback then skips the arity check, the new environment, or the return handling.
- Letting a Python exception escape: `sorted([1, "a"])` raises `TypeError`, and `int("x")` raises `ValueError`. Check types first and raise `CometError`.
- Accepting truthy results in `filter`, so a callback that returns a number quietly works.
- Walking the live list in `map` while the callback pushes to it.

::: context prelude A prelude
Haskell calls the definitions every program gets without importing anything "the Prelude", and the word spread. Much of Haskell's Prelude, Scheme's library and Python's standard modules are written in the language itself, while the core operations underneath are native. The split is a trade-off between speed and simplicity: CPython rewrote parts of its library in C when they were too slow, such as `heapq` and `collections.OrderedDict`.
:::

::: context reentrant Re-entrant code
Code is re-entrant if it can be entered again while an earlier entry has not finished, and still work. Recursion is the everyday case. Interrupt handlers in flight software are the hard case: the handler can fire in the middle of the code it interrupts. The usual rule is the same as this interpreter's: keep no hidden global state, or restore any you change on every way out.
:::

::: context mapreduce MapReduce
In 2004, Jeffrey Dean and Sanjay Ghemawat described MapReduce, the system Google used to process data spread over thousands of machines. A job is a map step, run in parallel on every piece of the input, and a reduce step that combines the results by key. The names come from the functional programming functions, and the key idea is the same one that makes Comet's `map` simple: the mapped function looks at one item at a time and changes nothing else, so the items can be processed in any order, or all at once.
:::
--- task
The starter gives the helpers `expect_function(name, value)` and `string_builtin`, and the builtins `type`, `str`, `abs`, `sum`, `min`, `max`, `reverse`, `repeat`, `upper`, `lower`, `trim`, `find`, `starts_with`, `ends_with` and `replace`. Write these builtins (their stubs are registered already); each checks its arguments with `expect_type` or `expect_function`, whose messages the checks expect:

- `range(n)` or `range(a, b)`: arity `(1, 2)`; int arguments; the list of ints from 0 (or `a`) up to but not including `n` (or `b`).
- `int(v)`: `v` must be an int or a str. An int comes back unchanged. A str may have spaces around it, then an optional `-`, then one or more ASCII digits; otherwise raise `cannot turn "TEXT" into an int` (the original text, written with `quote`).
- `sort(xs)`: a new list, sorted. `xs` must be a list whose items are all ints or all strs (an empty list is fine), otherwise `sort needs a list of all int or all str`.
- `map(xs, f)`, `filter(xs, f)`, `reduce(xs, f, start)`: `xs` a list and `f` a function (Comet or builtin), called with `interp.call(f, [args])`, over a copy of the list made before the first call. `filter`'s function must return a bool, otherwise `filter's function must return bool, not T`. `reduce` calls `f(running, item)`.
- `split(text, sep)`: two strs; an empty `sep` raises `split needs a separator that is not empty`; returns the pieces, empty ones included.
- `join(xs, sep)`: a list and a str; every item must be a str, otherwise `join needs a list of str`.
- `slice(value, start, end)`: a str or list and two ints; a negative position raises `slice positions cannot be negative`; returns the part from `start` up to `end`, with positions past the end cut back to it.
- `contains(container, item)`: a str or list; for a str, `item` must be a str and the answer is whether it is a substring; for a list, whether some item `values_equal`s it.
--- starter
"""Comet: a small programming language, built in layers.

    source text -> Lexer -> tokens -> Parser -> syntax tree
                -> Resolver -> Interpreter -> printed output

Each layer only talks to the one after it, so each can be tested alone.
"""
import operator
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


# ============================================================================
# Tokens and the lexer
# ============================================================================

KEYWORDS = {
    "let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "for", "in", "break",
    "continue", "print", "true", "false", "nil", "and", "or", "not",
}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){}[],;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = set("0123456789")
LETTERS = set("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_")
# Characters people type from other languages, and what Comet wants instead.
LEX_HINTS = {
    "'": "strings use double quotes",
    "&": "use 'and'",
    "|": "use 'or'",
    "!": "use 'not', or '!=' for not equal",
}


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str   # NUMBER, STRING, IDENT, KEYWORD, OP or EOF
    text: str   # the source text; for a STRING, the decoded value
    line: int   # counted from 1
    col: int    # counted from 1


class StaticError(Exception):
    """A mistake found before the program runs. Prints as "line:col: message"."""

    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.message = message
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


class LexError(StaticError):
    """A character sequence that is not a Comet token."""


class Lexer:
    """Turns source text into tokens. It keeps going after a mistake, so one
    scan reports every lexing error, each with its line and column."""

    def __init__(self, source):
        self.source = source
        self.pos = 0          # index of the next character to read
        self.line = 1         # where that character is, for messages
        self.col = 1
        self.tokens = []
        self.errors = []

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        """A character ahead of the read position, or "" past the end."""
        i = self.pos + ahead
        return self.source[i] if i < len(self.source) else ""

    def advance(self):
        """Consumes one character and keeps line and col in step with it."""
        ch = self.source[self.pos]
        self.pos += 1
        if ch == "\n":
            self.line += 1
            self.col = 1
        else:
            self.col += 1
        return ch

    def scan(self):
        """Returns (tokens, errors): every token ending with EOF, and every LexError."""
        while self.pos < len(self.source):
            self.scan_token()
        self.tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", self.line, self.col))
        return self.tokens, self.errors

    def scan_token(self):
        line, col = self.line, self.col
        ch = self.peek()
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            self.advance()
        elif ch == "#":
            while self.peek() not in ("", "\n"):
                self.advance()
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            self.number(line, col)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            self.word(line, col)
        elif ch == '"':
            self.string(line, col)
        elif ch + self.peek(1) in TWO_CHAR:
            text = self.advance() + self.advance()
            self.tokens.append(Token("OP", text, line, col))
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            self.tokens.append(Token("OP", self.advance(), line, col))
        else:
            self.advance()   # skip it, report it, and carry on
            message = f"unexpected character {ch!r}"
            if ch in LEX_HINTS:
                message += f" ({LEX_HINTS[ch]})"
            self.errors.append(LexError(message, line, col))

    def number(self, line, col):
        start = self.pos
        while self.peek() in DIGITS:
            self.advance()
        self.tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", self.source[start:self.pos], line, col))

    def word(self, line, col):
        start = self.pos
        while self.peek() in LETTERS or self.peek() in DIGITS:
            self.advance()
        text = self.source[start:self.pos]
        kind = "KEYWORD" if text in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
        self.tokens.append(Token(kind, text, line, col))

    def string(self, line, col):
        """A string literal. The token's text is the decoded value."""
        self.advance()  # the opening quote
        chars = []
        while True:
            ch = self.peek()
            if ch in ("", "\n"):
                # Strings never span lines, so the rest of this line is lost.
                self.errors.append(LexError("unterminated string", line, col))
                return
            if ch == '"':
                self.advance()
                break
            if ch == "\\":
                at_line, at_col = self.line, self.col
                self.advance()
                code = self.peek()
                if code in ESCAPES:
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[self.advance()])
                elif code not in ("", "\n"):
                    self.advance()
                    self.errors.append(LexError(f"unknown escape \\{code}", at_line, at_col))
                continue
            chars.append(self.advance())
        self.tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), line, col))


def tokenize(source):
    """The tokens of source; raises the first LexError if there is one."""
    tokens, errors = Lexer(source).scan()
    if errors:
        raise errors[0]
    return tokens


def point_at(source, line, col):
    """Two lines: source line `line`, and a caret under column `col`.
    Tabs before the column are copied, so the caret lines up in a terminal."""
    lines = source.split("\n")
    text = lines[line - 1] if 1 <= line <= len(lines) else ""
    pad = "".join("\t" if c == "\t" else " " for c in text[:col - 1])
    return text + "\n" + pad.ljust(col - 1) + "^"


# ============================================================================
# The syntax tree
# ============================================================================

def pos_field():
    """A node's line or column: given by keyword, and never part of ==."""
    return field(default=0, kw_only=True, compare=False, repr=False)


@dataclass
class Node:
