        return self.name


class BreakSignal(Exception):
    """Thrown by break; caught by the innermost loop."""


class ContinueSignal(Exception):
    """Thrown by continue; caught by the innermost loop, which goes on."""
SEQUENCES = ("list", "str")
SIZED = ("list", "str", "map")


def checked_index(seq, index):
    """index, after checking it is an int inside seq; else CometError."""
    if type_name(index) != "int":
        raise CometError(f"an index must be int, not {type_name(index)}")
    if not 0 <= index < len(seq):
        raise CometError(f"index {index} out of range for a {type_name(seq)} of length {len(seq)}")
    return index


def map_key(key):
    if type_name(key) != "str":
        raise CometError(f"map keys must be str, not {type_name(key)}")
    return key


def get_item(target, index):
    """target[index], with Comet's checks."""
    kind = type_name(target)
    if kind == "map":
        key = map_key(index)
        if key not in target:
            raise CometError(f"no key {quote(key)} in map")
        return target[key]
    if kind in SEQUENCES:
        return target[checked_index(target, index)]
    raise CometError(f"cannot index a value of type {kind}")


def set_item(target, index, value):
    """target[index] = value, with Comet's checks."""
    kind = type_name(target)
    if kind == "list":
        target[checked_index(target, index)] = value
    elif kind == "map":
        target[map_key(index)] = value
    elif kind == "str":
        raise CometError("strings cannot be changed; build a new one instead")
    else:
        raise CometError(f"cannot index a value of type {kind}")


def iteration(value):
    """The items a for loop walks through, as a list made before the loop
    starts: a body that changes the value cannot confuse the loop."""
    kind = type_name(value)
    if kind == "list":
        return list(value)
    if kind == "str":
        return list(value)          # one-character strings
    if kind == "map":
        return list(value.keys())   # the keys, in the order they were added
    raise CometError(f"cannot loop over a value of type {kind}")


# ============================================================================
# The standard library
# ============================================================================

BUILTINS = {}   # name -> (Python function, arity); every Interpreter defines them


def builtin(name, arity):
    """Registers the decorated Python function as a Comet builtin. arity is a
    number, or a (fewest, most) pair."""
    def register(fn):
        BUILTINS[name] = (fn, arity)
        return fn
    return register


def expect_type(name, value, *kinds):
    """Raises CometError unless value's type is one of kinds."""
    if type_name(value) not in kinds:
        wanted = kinds[0] if len(kinds) == 1 else ", ".join(kinds[:-1]) + " or " + kinds[-1]
        raise CometError(f"{name} needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")


@builtin("len", 1)
def builtin_len(interp, value):
    expect_type("len", value, *SIZED)
    return len(value)


@builtin("push", 2)
def builtin_push(interp, items, value):
    expect_type("push", items, "list")
    items.append(value)     # in place: every name for this list sees it
    return None


@builtin("items", 1)
def builtin_items(interp, table):
    """The map's [key, value] pairs, in the order the keys were added."""
    expect_type("items", table, "map")
    return [[key, value] for key, value in table.items()]


@builtin("ord", 1)
def builtin_ord(interp, char):
    expect_type("ord", char, "str")
    if len(char) != 1:
        raise CometError(f"ord needs a string of one character, not {len(char)}")
    return ord(char)


@builtin("chr", 1)
def builtin_chr(interp, code):
    expect_type("chr", code, "int")
    if not 0 <= code <= 0x10FFFF:
        raise CometError(f"chr needs a code from 0 to 1114111, not {code}")
    return chr(code)


@builtin("keys", 1)
def builtin_keys(interp, table):
    expect_type("keys", table, "map")
    return list(table)


@builtin("values", 1)
def builtin_values(interp, table):
    expect_type("values", table, "map")
    return list(table.values())


@builtin("has", 2)
def builtin_has(interp, table, key):
    expect_type("has", table, "map")
    return map_key(key) in table


@builtin("remove", 2)
def builtin_remove(interp, table, key):
    expect_type("remove", table, "map")
    key = map_key(key)
    if key not in table:
        raise CometError(f"no key {quote(key)} in map")
    return table.pop(key)


def expect_function(name, value):
    if type_name(value) != "fn":
        raise CometError(f"{name} needs a function, not {type_name(value)}")


@builtin("type", 1)
def builtin_type(interp, value):
    return type_name(value)


@builtin("str", 1)
def builtin_str(interp, value):
    return show(value)


@builtin("range", (1, 2))
def builtin_range(interp, *bounds):
    for bound in bounds:
        expect_type("range", bound, "int")
    return list(range(*bounds))


@builtin("int", 1)
def builtin_int(interp, value):
    expect_type("int", value, "int", "str")
    if type_name(value) == "int":
        return value
    text = value.strip()
    digits = text[1:] if text[:1] == "-" else text
    if not digits or any(c not in DIGITS for c in digits):
        raise CometError(f"cannot turn {quote(value)} into an int")
    return int(text)


@builtin("sort", 1)
def builtin_sort(interp, items):
    expect_type("sort", items, "list")
    kinds = {type_name(item) for item in items}
    if len(kinds) > 1 or kinds - {"int", "str"}:
        raise CometError("sort needs a list of all int or all str")
    return sorted(items)    # a new list; Python's sort is stable


@builtin("map", 2)
def builtin_map(interp, items, fn):
    expect_type("map", items, "list")
    expect_function("map", fn)
    return [interp.call(fn, [item]) for item in list(items)]


@builtin("filter", 2)
def builtin_filter(interp, items, fn):
    expect_type("filter", items, "list")
    expect_function("filter", fn)
    kept = []
    for item in list(items):
        keep = interp.call(fn, [item])
        if type_name(keep) != "bool":
            raise CometError(f"filter's function must return bool, not {type_name(keep)}")
        if keep:
            kept.append(item)
    return kept


@builtin("reduce", 3)
def builtin_reduce(interp, items, fn, start):
    expect_type("reduce", items, "list")
    expect_function("reduce", fn)
    total = start
    for item in list(items):
        total = interp.call(fn, [total, item])
    return total


@builtin("split", 2)
def builtin_split(interp, text, sep):
    expect_type("split", text, "str")
    expect_type("split", sep, "str")
    if sep == "":
        raise CometError("split needs a separator that is not empty")
    return text.split(sep)


@builtin("join", 2)
def builtin_join(interp, items, sep):
    expect_type("join", items, "list")
    expect_type("join", sep, "str")
    if any(type_name(item) != "str" for item in items):
        raise CometError("join needs a list of str")
    return sep.join(items)


@builtin("slice", 3)
def builtin_slice(interp, value, start, end):
    expect_type("slice", value, "str", "list")
    expect_type("slice", start, "int")
    expect_type("slice", end, "int")
    if start < 0 or end < 0:
        raise CometError("slice positions cannot be negative")
    return value[start:end]     # positions past the end are cut back to it


@builtin("contains", 2)
def builtin_contains(interp, container, item):
    expect_type("contains", container, "str", "list")
    if type_name(container) == "str":
        expect_type("contains", item, "str")
        return item in container
    return any(values_equal(x, item) for x in container)


def string_builtin(name, method):
    """A builtin that takes one str and returns str.method()."""
    def fn(interp, text):
        expect_type(name, text, "str")
        return getattr(text, method)()
    builtin(name, 1)(fn)


@builtin("abs", 1)
def builtin_abs(interp, n):
    expect_type("abs", n, "int")
    return abs(n)


def numbers(name, items):
    expect_type(name, items, "list")
    if any(type_name(item) != "int" for item in items):
        raise CometError(f"{name} needs a list of int")
    return items


@builtin("sum", 1)
def builtin_sum(interp, items):
    return sum(numbers("sum", items))


@builtin("min", 1)
def builtin_min(interp, items):
    if not numbers("min", items):
        raise CometError("min of an empty list")
    return min(items)


@builtin("max", 1)
def builtin_max(interp, items):
    if not numbers("max", items):
        raise CometError("max of an empty list")
    return max(items)


@builtin("reverse", 1)
def builtin_reverse(interp, value):
    expect_type("reverse", value, "list", "str")
    return value[::-1]


@builtin("repeat", 2)
def builtin_repeat(interp, text, times):
    expect_type("repeat", text, "str")
    expect_type("repeat", times, "int")
    if times < 0:
        raise CometError("repeat needs a count of 0 or more")
    return text * times


string_builtin("upper", "upper")
string_builtin("lower", "lower")
string_builtin("trim", "strip")


@builtin("find", 2)
def builtin_find(interp, text, part):
    expect_type("find", text, "str")
    expect_type("find", part, "str")
    return text.find(part)


@builtin("starts_with", 2)
def builtin_starts_with(interp, text, prefix):
    expect_type("starts_with", text, "str")
    expect_type("starts_with", prefix, "str")
    return text.startswith(prefix)


@builtin("ends_with", 2)
def builtin_ends_with(interp, text, suffix):
    expect_type("ends_with", text, "str")
    expect_type("ends_with", suffix, "str")
    return text.endswith(suffix)


@builtin("replace", 3)
def builtin_replace(interp, text, old, new):
    for value in (text, old, new):
        expect_type("replace", value, "str")
    if old == "":
        raise CometError("replace needs an old part that is not empty")
    return text.replace(old, new)


# ============================================================================
# The interpreter
# ============================================================================


class Environment:
    """One scope's variables, and the scope around it (None for the globals)."""

    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        self.values = {}
        self.parent = parent

    def define(self, name, value):
        if self.parent is not None and name in self.values:
            raise CometError(f"{name} is already declared in this scope")
        self.values[name] = value

    def lookup(self, name):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                return env.values[name]
            env = env.parent
        raise CometError(f"undefined variable {name}")

    def assign(self, name, value):
        env = self
        while env is not None:
            if name in env.values:
                env.values[name] = value
                return
            env = env.parent
        raise CometError(f"assignment to undeclared variable {name}")

    def ancestor(self, depth):
        """The scope `depth` steps out from this one."""
        env = self
        for _ in range(depth):
            env = env.parent
        return env


class Interpreter:
    """Runs a syntax tree. Printed lines collect in self.output."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.globals = Environment()
        self.env = self.globals       # the scope running now
        self.output = []
        for name, (fn, arity) in BUILTINS.items():
            self.globals.define(name, Builtin(name, fn, arity))

    def run(self, program):
        for stmt in program.stmts:
            self.execute(stmt)

    def handler(self, prefix, node):
        """The method for this kind of node: exec_Print for a Print, and so on."""
        method = getattr(self, prefix + type(node).__name__, None)
        if method is None:
            raise CometError(f"{type(node).__name__} is not supported yet")
        return method

    def execute(self, stmt):
        self.handler("exec_", stmt)(stmt)

    def evaluate(self, expr):
        return self.handler("eval_", expr)(expr)

    def execute_block(self, stmts, env):
        """Runs stmts with env as the current scope, and always puts the old
        scope back, also when a statement raises."""
        previous = self.env
        self.env = env
        try:
            for stmt in stmts:
                self.execute(stmt)
        finally:
            self.env = previous

    # ---- statements ----

    def exec_Let(self, stmt):
        self.env.define(stmt.name, self.evaluate(stmt.expr))

    def exec_Assign(self, stmt):
        value = self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        if stmt.depth is None:
            self.globals.assign(stmt.name, value)
        else:
            self.env.ancestor(stmt.depth).values[stmt.name] = value

    def exec_Print(self, stmt):
        self.output.append(show(self.evaluate(stmt.expr)))

    def exec_ExprStmt(self, stmt):
        self.evaluate(stmt.expr)

    def exec_If(self, stmt):
        if self.condition(stmt.cond):
            self.execute(stmt.then)
        elif stmt.else_ is not None:
            self.execute(stmt.else_)    # a Block, or an If for "else if"

    def exec_While(self, stmt):
        while self.condition(stmt.cond):
            try:
                self.execute(stmt.body)
            except BreakSignal:
                break
            except ContinueSignal:
                pass

    def exec_Block(self, stmt):
        self.execute_block(stmt.stmts, Environment(self.env))

    def condition(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise CometError(f"a condition must be bool, not {type_name(value)}")
        return value

    # ---- expressions ----

    def eval_Num(self, expr):
        return expr.value

    eval_Str = eval_Bool = eval_Num

    def eval_Nil(self, expr):
        return None

    def eval_Var(self, expr):
        if expr.depth is None:
            return self.globals.lookup(expr.name)
        return self.env.ancestor(expr.depth).values[expr.name]

    def eval_Unary(self, expr):
        value = self.evaluate(expr.expr)
        if expr.op == "-":
            self.need("int", value, "-")
            return -value
        self.need("bool", value, "not")
        return not value

    def need(self, wanted, value, op):
        if type_name(value) != wanted:
            raise CometError(f"'{op}' needs {wanted}, not {type_name(value)}")

    def eval_Binary(self, expr):
        op = expr.op
        left = self.evaluate(expr.left)
        if op in ("and", "or"):
            self.need("bool", left, op)
            if left == (op == "or"):     # false and ..., true or ...: already decided
                return left
            right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
            self.need("bool", right, op)
            return right
        right = self.evaluate(expr.right)
        if op in ("==", "!="):
            lt, rt = type_name(left), type_name(right)
            if lt != rt and "nil" not in (lt, rt):
                raise CometError(f"cannot compare {lt} with {rt}")
            return values_equal(left, right) == (op == "==")
        return arithmetic(op, left, right)

    # ---- functions ----

    def exec_Fn(self, stmt):
        self.env.define(stmt.name, Closure(stmt, self.env))

    def eval_FnExpr(self, expr):
        return Closure(expr, self.env)

    def exec_Return(self, stmt):
        value = None if stmt.expr is None else self.evaluate(stmt.expr)
        raise ReturnSignal(value)

    def eval_Call(self, expr):
        callee = self.evaluate(expr.callee)
        args = [self.evaluate(arg) for arg in expr.args]
        return self.call(callee, args)

    def call(self, callee, args):
        """Calls a function value with argument values, and returns its result."""
        if isinstance(callee, Closure):
            params = callee.decl.params
            check_arity(callee.label(), len(params), len(params), len(args))
            env = Environment(callee.env)   # inside the fn's own scope, not the caller's
            for (name, _type), value in zip(params, args):
                env.define(name, value)
            try:
                self.execute_block(callee.decl.body.stmts, env)
            except ReturnSignal as signal:
                return signal.value
            return None
        if isinstance(callee, Builtin):
            check_arity(callee.name, callee.fewest, callee.most, len(args))
            return callee.fn(self, *args)
        raise CometError(f"cannot call a value of type {type_name(callee)}")

    # ---- lists, loops and jumps ----

    def eval_ListLit(self, expr):
        return [self.evaluate(item) for item in expr.items]

    def eval_Index(self, expr):
        target = self.evaluate(expr.target)
        return get_item(target, self.evaluate(expr.index))

    def exec_SetIndex(self, stmt):
        target = self.evaluate(stmt.target)
        index = self.evaluate(stmt.index)
        set_item(target, index, self.evaluate(stmt.expr))

    def exec_For(self, stmt):
        for item in iteration(self.evaluate(stmt.iterable)):
            env = Environment(self.env)     # a fresh variable for every pass
            env.define(stmt.name, item)
            try:
                self.execute_block(stmt.body.stmts, env)
            except BreakSignal:
                break
            except ContinueSignal:
                pass

    def exec_Break(self, stmt):
        raise BreakSignal()

    def exec_Continue(self, stmt):
        raise ContinueSignal()

    def eval_MapLit(self, expr):
        table = {}
        for key, value in expr.pairs:
            table[map_key(self.evaluate(key))] = self.evaluate(value)
        return table


def run(source):
    """Runs a Comet program and returns what it printed, one line per print.
    Errors found before running are the whole answer; a runtime error is
    added after whatever was printed before it."""
    program, errors = parse(source)
    if not errors:
        errors = resolve(program)
    if errors:
        return "\n".join(str(e) for e in errors)
    interp = Interpreter()
    try:
        interp.run(program)
    except CometError as e:
        interp.output.append(f"runtime error: {e}")
    return "\n".join(interp.output)
--- hint
Most are three or four lines: `expect_type` for each argument, then one line of Python (`list(range(*bounds))`, `sorted(items)`, `text.split(sep)`, `sep.join(items)`, `value[start:end]`). Look at the given `builtin_find` for the pattern.
--- hint
For `sort`, collect the set of item type names: it is fine if it has at most one element and that element is `int` or `str`. For `int`, strip the text, remove one leading `-`, and check that what is left is non-empty and made only of characters in `DIGITS`.
--- hint
The higher-order three loop over `list(items)` and call `interp.call(fn, [item])` (or `[total, item]` for `reduce`). `filter` checks each result with `type_name(keep) != "bool"` before using it.

+++ practice | A command table built with a decorator
--- task
A ground-station console runs commands typed as words, such as `add 2 3`. Write a decorator `command(name, arity)` that registers the function below it in the dict `COMMANDS` (name to `(function, arity)`) and returns the function unchanged, and `dispatch(line)`, which splits the line on spaces, looks up the first word, converts the other words to ints, and returns the function's result.

`dispatch` raises `KeyError` with the message `unknown command NAME` for an unknown name, and `TypeError` with `NAME expects N arguments, got M` for the wrong number of arguments. Register two commands with your decorator: `add` (2 arguments, their sum) and `neg` (1 argument, its negation).

For example, `dispatch("add 2 3")` is 5 and `dispatch("neg 4")` is -4.
--- starter
COMMANDS = {}


def dispatch(line):
    return 0
--- solution
COMMANDS = {}


def command(name, arity):
    def register(fn):
        COMMANDS[name] = (fn, arity)
        return fn
    return register


@command("add", 2)
def add(a, b):
    return a + b


@command("neg", 1)
def neg(a):
    return -a


def dispatch(line):
    name, *words = line.split()
    if name not in COMMANDS:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown command {name}")
    fn, arity = COMMANDS[name]
    if len(words) != arity:
        raise TypeError(f"{name} expects {arity} arguments, got {len(words)}")
    return fn(*[int(w) for w in words])
--- hint
A decorator with arguments is a function that returns the real decorator: `command(name, arity)` returns `register(fn)`, which stores the function and returns it.
--- hint
`name, *words = line.split()` splits off the first word. Check the name, then the count, then call with `*` to spread the converted arguments.
--- check case | The examples
(dispatch("add 2 3"), dispatch("neg 4"), dispatch("add -1 1"))
=> (5, -4, 0)
--- check test | The decorator returns the function unchanged and registers it
command("twice", 1)(lambda x: 2 * x)(21) == 42 and dispatch("twice 5") == 10 and COMMANDS["add"][1] == 2
--- check test | Unknown commands and wrong counts
raises(KeyError, lambda: dispatch("jump 1")) and __import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(TypeError, "^add expects 2 arguments, got 1$", dispatch, "add 1") is None and __import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(TypeError, "^neg expects 1 arguments, got 0$", dispatch, "neg") is None

+++ practice | range with a step
--- task
Write `comet_range(*args)` like Python's `range`, returning a list, but with Comet-style checks. It takes 1 to 3 arguments: `(stop)`, `(start, stop)` or `(start, stop, step)`, with a default start of 0 and step of 1. A negative step counts down, as in Python.

Raise `TypeError` with `range expects 1 to 3 arguments, got N` for a wrong count, and `range needs int, not T` for an argument that is not an int (bools are not ints; T is the Python type name, such as `bool`, `str` or `float`). Raise `ValueError` with `range step cannot be zero`.

For example, `comet_range(10, 0, -3)` is `[10, 7, 4, 1]`.
--- starter
def comet_range(*args):
    return list(range(*args))
--- solution
def comet_range(*args):
    if not 1 <= len(args) <= 3:
        raise TypeError(f"range expects 1 to 3 arguments, got {len(args)}")
    for a in args:
        if isinstance(a, bool) or not isinstance(a, int):
            raise TypeError(f"range needs int, not {type(a).__name__}")
    start, stop, step = (0, args[0], 1) if len(args) == 1 else (*args, 1)[:3]
    if step == 0:
        raise ValueError("range step cannot be zero")
    out = []
    i = start
    while (step > 0 and i < stop) or (step < 0 and i > stop):
        out.append(i)
        i += step
    return out
--- hint
Check the count, then each argument's type (reject bools explicitly), then fill in the defaults and check the step.
--- hint
Counting up stops when the value reaches `stop` or passes it; counting down stops when it reaches or goes below it.
--- check case | The example and the usual forms
(comet_range(10, 0, -3), comet_range(4), comet_range(2, 5), comet_range(0, 10, 4))
=> ([10, 7, 4, 1], [0, 1, 2, 3], [2, 3, 4], [0, 4, 8])
--- check case | Empty ranges
(comet_range(0), comet_range(5, 2), comet_range(2, 5, -1), comet_range(-3))
=> ([], [], [], [])
--- check test | Wrong counts and types
__import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(TypeError, "^range expects 1 to 3 arguments, got 0$", comet_range) is None and __import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(TypeError, "^range needs int, not bool$", comet_range, True) is None and __import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(TypeError, "^range needs int, not float$", comet_range, 1, 2.5) is None and raises(TypeError, lambda: comet_range(1, 2, 3, 4))
--- check test | A zero step
__import__("unittest").TestCase().assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "^range step cannot be zero$", comet_range, 1, 5, 0) is None

+++ practice | Sorting by a key function
--- task
Write `sort_by(items, key)` that returns a new list of the items sorted by `key(item)`, from smallest to largest, keeping items with equal keys in their original order. `key` is a Python function. Every key must be an int (not a bool) or every key must be a string; otherwise raise `TypeError` with `keys must be all int or all str`. `items` must not change.

Call `key` exactly once per item. For example, `sort_by(["ccc", "a", "bb"], len)` is `["a", "bb", "ccc"]`.
--- starter
def sort_by(items, key):
    return sorted(items)
--- solution
def sort_by(items, key):
    keys = [key(item) for item in items]
    kinds = {"bool" if isinstance(k, bool) else type(k).__name__ for k in keys}
    if len(kinds) > 1 or kinds - {"int", "str"}:
        raise TypeError("keys must be all int or all str")
    order = sorted(range(len(items)), key=lambda i: keys[i])
    return [items[i] for i in order]
--- hint
Compute all the keys first, once each, and check their types before sorting.
--- hint
Sort the positions `0 … n − 1` by their keys: Python's `sorted` is stable, so equal keys keep their order.
--- check case | The example, and stability
(sort_by(["ccc", "a", "bb"], len), sort_by(["bb", "a", "cc", "d"], len))
=> (["a", "bb", "ccc"], ["a", "d", "bb", "cc"])
--- check case | String keys and an empty list
(sort_by([("vega", 3), ("altair", 1)], lambda p: p[0]), sort_by([], len))
=> ([("altair", 1), ("vega", 3)], [])
--- check test | The key is called once per item, and items is unchanged
(lambda calls, xs: (sort_by(xs, lambda x: calls.append(x) or -x), calls == [3, 1, 2] and xs == [3, 1, 2])[1])([], [3, 1, 2])
--- check test | Mixed or unsortable keys

+++ practice | A strict string-to-int conversion
--- task
Write `to_int(text)` that converts a string to an int with Comet's strict rules: spaces (and tabs and newlines) around the number are allowed, then an optional `-`, then one or more ASCII digits `0` to `9`, and nothing else. Raise `ValueError` with `cannot turn TEXT into an int`, where TEXT is the original argument written with Python's `repr`.

For example, `to_int(" -042 ")` is -42, and `to_int("1_000")` raises `ValueError: cannot turn '1_000' into an int`.
--- starter
def to_int(text):
    return int(text)
--- solution
DIGITS = set("0123456789")


def to_int(text):
    body = text.strip()
    digits = body[1:] if body.startswith("-") else body
    if not digits or any(c not in DIGITS for c in digits):
        raise ValueError(f"cannot turn {text!r} into an int")
    return int(body)
--- hint
Strip the spaces, take off one leading `-`, and check that what is left is not empty and is made only of the ten ASCII digits.
--- hint
Python's `int()` accepts underscores, a `+` sign and non-ASCII digits, so check before you convert.

+++ practice | Debug: split loses the last piece
--- task
`split(text, sep)` is written by hand. It should work like Python's `str.split` with a separator: every occurrence of `sep` cuts the string, and empty pieces are kept, so `split("a,b,", ",")` is `["a", "b", ""]` and `split("", ",")` is `[""]`. It loses the last piece whenever the text ends with the separator, and returns `[]` for an empty text. Find the bug and fix it.
--- starter
def split(text, sep):
    pieces = []
    start = 0
    i = 0
    while i <= len(text) - len(sep):
        if text[i:i + len(sep)] == sep:
            pieces.append(text[start:i])
            i += len(sep)
            start = i
        else:
            i += 1
    if start < len(text):
        pieces.append(text[start:])
    return pieces
--- solution
def split(text, sep):
    pieces = []
    start = 0
    i = 0
    while i <= len(text) - len(sep):
        if text[i:i + len(sep)] == sep:
            pieces.append(text[start:i])
            i += len(sep)
            start = i
        else:
            i += 1
    pieces.append(text[start:])
    return pieces
--- hint
After the loop, what is the last piece when the text ends with the separator? Should it be kept?
--- hint
There is always exactly one more piece than there are separators, even when that last piece is empty.
--- check case | Trailing and leading separators
(split("a,b,", ","), split(",a", ","), split(",", ","))
=> (["a", "b", ""], ["", "a"], ["", ""])
--- check case | Empty text and no separator
(split("", ","), split("abc", ";"))
=> ([""], ["abc"])
--- check case | Longer separators and neighbouring separators
(split("a::b::::c", "::"), split("x--", "--"))
=> (["a", "b", "", "c"], ["x", ""])

+++ practice | A template formatter
--- task
Write `format_text(template, values)` that fills a template such as `"{name} is at stage {stage}"` from the dict `values`. Each `{key}` is replaced by `str(values[key])`. `{{` stands for a literal `{` and `}}` for a literal `}`. Raise `KeyError` with the key for a key that is not in `values`, and `ValueError` for a `{` that is never closed, an empty `{}`, or a single `}` that is not part of `}}`.

For example, `format_text("{name} is at stage {stage}", {"name": "Vega", "stage": 2})` is `"Vega is at stage 2"`, and `format_text("{{literal}}", {})` is `"{literal}"`.
--- starter
def format_text(template, values):
    return template
--- solution
def format_text(template, values):
    out = []
    i = 0
    n = len(template)
    while i < n:
        ch = template[i]
        if ch == "{" and template[i + 1:i + 2] == "{":
            out.append("{")
            i += 2
        elif ch == "}" and template[i + 1:i + 2] == "}":
            out.append("}")
            i += 2
        elif ch == "{":
            end = template.find("}", i + 1)
            if end == -1:
                raise ValueError(f"unclosed '{{' at {i}")
            key = template[i + 1:end]
            if not key:
                raise ValueError(f"empty '{{}}' at {i}")
            if key not in values:
                raise KeyError(key)
            out.append(str(values[key]))
            i = end + 1
        elif ch == "}":
            raise ValueError(f"single '}}' at {i}")
        else:
            out.append(ch)
            i += 1
    return "".join(out)
--- hint
Walk the template with an index. Check for the two-character escapes `{{` and `}}` before treating a brace as the start of a key.
--- hint
Collect the pieces in a list and join them once at the end: the fast way to build a string.
--- check case | The examples
(format_text("{name} is at stage {stage}", {"name": "Vega", "stage": 2}), format_text("{{literal}}", {}))
=> ("Vega is at stage 2", "{literal}")
--- check case | Keys next to each other, repeated, and escapes around them
format_text("{a}{b}{a} {{{a}}}", {"a": 1, "b": "x"})
=> "1x1 {1}"
--- check case | No placeholders
(format_text("", {}), format_text("plain", {"x": 1}))
=> ("", "plain")
--- check test | Missing keys and bad braces
raises(KeyError, lambda: format_text("{nope}", {})) and all(raises(ValueError, lambda t=t: format_text(t, {"a": 1})) for t in ["{a", "{}", "a}", "}{a}"])

=== cap-interp-10 | Runtime errors with a call-stack trace
--- teach
Comet programs can now be real programs: many functions calling each other, callbacks inside library calls, data in lists and maps. And when one of them fails, the whole report is `runtime error: division by zero`. Which division? In which function? Called from where? This milestone makes runtime errors as useful as syntax errors: a **position** for every error, a **call-stack trace** showing the chain of calls that led to it, a clean `stack overflow` error instead of a Python crash, a "did you mean" hint for misspelt names, and an `error` builtin so Comet programs can fail on purpose.

Here is the goal. For this program:

```text
fn half(n) {
  return 10 / n;
}
fn average(n) {
  return half(n) + 1;
}
print "before";
print average(0);
```

`run` returns:

```text
before
runtime error at 2:13: division by zero
  in half (called at 5:10)
  in average (called at 8:7)
```

The first line says what went wrong and exactly where: the `/` on line 2. Each following line is one **frame** of the call stack, innermost first: the error happened inside `half`, which was called on line 5 by `average`, which was called on line 8 by the top level.

### Where an error happened

Every node has had a position since milestone 2, and every `CometError` is raised somewhere inside the evaluation of some node. The question is which node to blame. The rule: **the innermost node that was being evaluated**, because that is the most precise. In `print 1 + xs[5];`, the failing node is the index, not the `+` and not the `print`.

The mechanism is small. `CometError` gains `line`, `col` (0 while unknown) and a method `locate(node)`, which sets the position **only if it has none yet**. `evaluate` and `execute` each wrap their dispatch in a `try`, and on a `CometError` they call `e.locate(node)` and re-raise. The error travels outwards through every node that contains the failing one, and the first `locate`, at the innermost node, is the only one that takes effect. The helpers that raise errors, like `arithmetic` and `get_item`, do not need to know about positions at all.

A located error prints as `line:col: message` with `str()`, like a static error.

An error raised inside a builtin, such as `len(5)`, has no node of its own, so it is blamed on the call's node, whose position is the callee's.

### The call stack

The interpreter keeps a list, `self.frames`, of the names of the calls running now, outermost first; the Compilers course used the same name. `call` pushes the callee's name before running it and pops it afterwards, in a `finally`, so the list is right after an error too. That list is what makes the next two features possible.

Every error that comes up through a call gets that call's frame added to its **trace**, a list of lines stored on the error: `call` catches the `CometError`, appends `in NAME (called at L:C)` using the call site's position, and re-raises. As the error travels out through more calls, more lines are appended, so the trace ends up [[innermost first|tracebacks]], which is how the report prints it.

A call made by a builtin, such as `map` calling its callback, has no call site in the source. For those, `call` gets no node, and the frame says who called instead: `in anonymous fn (called by map)`. So the new signature is `call(callee, args, site=None)`: `eval_Call` passes its node, and builtins leave it out, exactly as they already do.

### Stack overflow, as a Comet error

A runaway recursion used to crash with Python's `RecursionError`, a [[stack overflow|overflow]]: the host language's limit leaking through. Each Comet call costs up to about twenty Python frames inside the interpreter (`call`, `invoke`, `execute_block`, `execute`, the statement method, `evaluate`, the expression methods, down to the next call), and Python stops at about a thousand, fewer in the browser. So Comet must stop **first**, with an error of its own: before pushing a frame, `call` checks the depth and raises `stack overflow: more than 40 calls deep` when 40 calls are already running. `MAX_DEPTH = 40` is the course's limit too, well inside Python's. `run` still catches `RecursionError` as a last safety net, but it should never be needed.

A deep enough recursion produces a trace with forty lines, almost all the same. That helps nobody, so the report **collapses repeats**: when a block of 1 to 4 lines repeats more than 3 times in a row, keep 3 copies and replace the rest with one line saying how many more there were. For `fn countdown(n) { return countdown(n - 1); }` on line 1, called by `countdown(3);` on line 3, the trace part of the report is:

```text
  in countdown (called at 1:26)
  in countdown (called at 1:26)
  in countdown (called at 1:26)
  ... the line above, 36 more times
  in countdown (called at 3:1)
```

Those are the 40 calls that were running: the first one from line 3, and 39 recursive calls from line 1, column 26. The call after them is the one that was refused.

Blocks longer than one line matter for mutual recursion, where the frames alternate between two functions: then the message is `... the 2 lines above, 16 more times`. When blocks of several sizes repeat at the same point, choose the one that removes the most lines. Python's own tracebacks do the one-line version of this, with "[Previous line repeated 996 more times]".

### Did you mean?

`undefined variable lenn` is accurate but unhelpful; `undefined variable lenn (did you mean len?)` fixes the bug. When a lookup or an assignment fails, the environment collects every name visible from it and picks the **closest** one by [[edit distance|levenshtein]]: the fewest single-character inserts, deletes or changes that turn one string into the other. `lenn` is 1 away from `len`. The distance is computed by dynamic programming, as in DSA II: a table where each cell is the distance between two prefixes, filled one row at a time.

A suggestion is only useful when it is likely to be right, so it is offered only when the distance is at most a third of the name's length (and at least 1), and among equally close names the alphabetically first wins, so the message is deterministic. Since the resolver already handles locals, an undefined name at run time is always looked up in the globals, which include every builtin: misspelt library calls are exactly the common case.

### error(), for Comet programs

The builtin `error(message)` raises a `CometError` with the program's own message. A Comet program can now reject bad input with a real error, located and traced like any other.

### The report

`error_report(error)` builds the lines `run` adds: `runtime error at L:C: MESSAGE`, or `runtime error: MESSAGE` when the error has no position, then each collapsed trace line indented by two spaces. `run` uses it instead of the one-line message.

### Designs considered

- **Building the trace from `self.frames` at the moment of the error**, instead of while unwinding. That works too, but the frames list has no call positions, and the error would need access to the interpreter. Appending in `call` as the error passes is simpler and puts each line where the information is.
- **Raising positions directly**, `CometError(msg, node.line, node.col)` at every raise. That spreads position handling across every helper, and helpers such as `arithmetic` do not have a node. `locate` keeps it in two places.
- **A larger limit**, by raising Python's recursion limit with `sys.setrecursionlimit`. That trades a clean error for a risk of crashing the whole process, and in a browser the real stack is smaller still. The real fix is an interpreter that does not use the host's stack at all, such as a bytecode VM with its own stack, which the Compilers course built.

### Why it is correct

- **Position:** a `CometError` passes through the `evaluate` or `execute` of every node that contains the node where it was raised, innermost first, and only the first `locate` changes anything. So the reported position is the innermost node that has one.
- **Trace:** each running call appends exactly one line when an error passes through it, in the order the calls are left, which is innermost first. `finally` pops each frame however the call ends, so `self.frames` always lists exactly the calls running now, even after errors, and later milestones that catch errors can rely on it.
- **Overflow:** a call is refused when 40 calls are running, so there are never more than 40 frames, and Python's stack is never exhausted by Comet calls.

### What it costs

When nothing goes wrong, almost nothing: a `try` costs nothing in Python 3.11 and later until an exception is raised, and a frame is one list append and one pop per call. When an error does happen, each frame adds a line to the trace, O(depth). Edit distance costs O(len(a) × len(b)) per candidate name, only when an error is being reported, over the few dozen global names.

### How to test it

Exact reports for: an error two calls deep; an error at the top level (no trace); an error inside a callback called by a builtin; an error inside a builtin; a runaway recursion (collapsed); a mutual recursion (collapsed in pairs); `error()`; a misspelt name with and without a close suggestion. Then the helpers on their own: `collapse`, `edit_distance`, `closest`, `error_report`.

### Where it is used

- Every mainstream runtime prints a stack trace on an uncaught error: Python's traceback, Java's stack trace, JavaScript's `error.stack`. It is usually the first thing anyone reads when a program fails.
- Rust, Elm and recent versions of Python suggest similar names for misspellings, using edit distance.
- Flight software records a trace of the failing task, often into non-volatile memory, so engineers on the ground can see the call chain of a fault that happened far away.

**Watch out:** trace bugs.

- Setting the position at every level instead of only the first: the error then points at the outermost `print`, not at the division.
- Popping the frame outside a `finally`: after the first caught error the frames list is wrong for ever, and a later milestone that catches errors reports stack overflows that did not happen.
- Checking the depth after pushing, which allows one extra call or counts wrongly.
- Collapsing repeats that are not adjacent: only runs in a row may be collapsed, or the trace misrepresents the calls.


::: context tracebacks Reading a traceback
Python prints its traceback outermost first and the error last, because the most recent call is then next to the prompt. Java and JavaScript print the innermost frame first, as Comet does, because that is where the error happened. Both orders carry the same information; what matters is that each frame says which function and which line. When a trace is long, the frames closest to your own code are usually the ones to read first.
:::

::: context overflow Stack overflows in the wild
A stack overflow happens when nested calls use up the memory set aside for the call stack. In C it is not an error message but a crash, or worse, silent corruption of whatever memory lies beyond the stack. Safety standards for flight and medical software, such as MISRA C and NASA's "Power of Ten" rules, forbid recursion outright, so that the maximum stack depth can be proved before the code ever runs.
:::


::: context levenshtein Edit distance
Vladimir Levenshtein defined this distance in 1965, for error-correcting codes. The standard algorithm fills a table where the cell for the first i characters of one word and the first j of the other is the smallest of three neighbours plus one: delete a character, insert one, or change one (free if the characters already match). Spell checkers, DNA sequence alignment and "did you mean" in search engines all use it or its relatives. The stretch practice problem adds transposition, swapping two neighbouring letters, which is the commonest typing mistake of all.
:::
--- task
Write:

- `CometError(message, line=0, col=0)`, with attributes `message`, `line`, `col` and `trace` (a list, empty at first); `locate(node)` sets `line` and `col` from the node only if `line` is still 0 and the node's `line` is not; `str()` gives `L:C: MESSAGE` when located, else the message.
- `evaluate` and `execute` call `locate` on every `CometError` passing through them, then re-raise.
- `MAX_DEPTH = 40`, and `Interpreter.__init__` sets `self.frames = []` and `self.max_depth = MAX_DEPTH`.
- `call(callee, args, site=None)`: a value that is not a `Closure` or `Builtin` raises `cannot call a value of type T`. If `len(self.frames) >= self.max_depth`, raise `stack overflow: more than N calls deep` (N is `max_depth`). Otherwise push `callee.label()` on `self.frames`, run the call, and pop it in a `finally`. A `CometError` coming out of the call gets `in NAME (CALLER)` appended to its `trace`, where CALLER is `called at L:C` (the site's position), or `called by OUTER` (the name on top of `self.frames` before the push) when `site` is `None`, or `called by the interpreter` when there is no frame either. Put the old body of `call` in a method `invoke(callee, args)`. `eval_Call` passes its node as `site`.
- `edit_distance(a, b)`: the Levenshtein distance. `closest(name, candidates)`: the candidate with the smallest distance to `name`, if that distance is at most `max(1, len(name) // 3)`; ties go to the alphabetically first; `None` if none qualifies.
- `Environment.lookup` and `assign`: when the name is not found, add ` (did you mean X?)` to the message, where X is `closest(name, every name visible from this environment outwards)`, or add nothing if there is none.
- `collapse(lines, keep=3, longest=4)`: at each position, among block sizes 1 to `longest`, find how many times the block starting there repeats in a row; if some block repeats more than `keep` times, take the one that covers the most lines, output its first `keep` copies and then `... the line above, N more times` (size 1) or `... the S lines above, N more times`, and continue after the whole run; otherwise output the line and move on.
- `error_report(error)`: `runtime error at L:C: MESSAGE` (or `runtime error: MESSAGE` without a position), followed by each line of `collapse(error.trace)` with two spaces in front. `run` extends the output with it for a `CometError`, and appends `runtime error: stack overflow` for a `RecursionError`.
- A builtin `error(message)` (arity 1) that raises `CometError(message)`; the message must be a str (`expect_type`).
--- starter
"""Comet: a small programming language, built in layers.

    source text -> Lexer -> tokens -> Parser -> syntax tree
                -> Resolver -> Interpreter -> printed output

Each layer only talks to the one after it, so each can be tested alone.
"""
import operator
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


# ============================================================================
# Tokens and the lexer
# ============================================================================

KEYWORDS = {
    "let", "fn", "return", "if", "else", "while", "for", "in", "break",
    "continue", "print", "true", "false", "nil", "and", "or", "not",
}
TWO_CHAR = {"==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "->"}
ONE_CHAR = set("+-*/%<>=(){}[],;:")
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n"}
DIGITS = set("0123456789")
LETTERS = set("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_")
# Characters people type from other languages, and what Comet wants instead.
LEX_HINTS = {
    "'": "strings use double quotes",
    "&": "use 'and'",
    "|": "use 'or'",
    "!": "use 'not', or '!=' for not equal",
}


@dataclass
class Token:
    kind: str   # NUMBER, STRING, IDENT, KEYWORD, OP or EOF
    text: str   # the source text; for a STRING, the decoded value
    line: int   # counted from 1
    col: int    # counted from 1


class StaticError(Exception):
    """A mistake found before the program runs. Prints as "line:col: message"."""

    def __init__(self, message, line, col):
        super().__init__(f"{line}:{col}: {message}")
        self.message = message
        self.line = line
        self.col = col


class LexError(StaticError):
    """A character sequence that is not a Comet token."""


class Lexer:
    """Turns source text into tokens. It keeps going after a mistake, so one
    scan reports every lexing error, each with its line and column."""

    def __init__(self, source):
        self.source = source
        self.pos = 0          # index of the next character to read
        self.line = 1         # where that character is, for messages
        self.col = 1
        self.tokens = []
        self.errors = []

    def peek(self, ahead=0):
        """A character ahead of the read position, or "" past the end."""
        i = self.pos + ahead
        return self.source[i] if i < len(self.source) else ""

    def advance(self):
        """Consumes one character and keeps line and col in step with it."""
        ch = self.source[self.pos]
        self.pos += 1
        if ch == "\n":
            self.line += 1
            self.col = 1
        else:
            self.col += 1
        return ch

    def scan(self):
        """Returns (tokens, errors): every token ending with EOF, and every LexError."""
        while self.pos < len(self.source):
            self.scan_token()
        self.tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", self.line, self.col))
        return self.tokens, self.errors

    def scan_token(self):
        line, col = self.line, self.col
        ch = self.peek()
        if ch in " \t\r\n":
            self.advance()
        elif ch == "#":
            while self.peek() not in ("", "\n"):
                self.advance()
        elif ch in DIGITS:
            self.number(line, col)
        elif ch in LETTERS:
            self.word(line, col)
        elif ch == '"':
            self.string(line, col)
        elif ch + self.peek(1) in TWO_CHAR:
            text = self.advance() + self.advance()
            self.tokens.append(Token("OP", text, line, col))
        elif ch in ONE_CHAR:
            self.tokens.append(Token("OP", self.advance(), line, col))
        else:
            self.advance()   # skip it, report it, and carry on
            message = f"unexpected character {ch!r}"
            if ch in LEX_HINTS:
                message += f" ({LEX_HINTS[ch]})"
            self.errors.append(LexError(message, line, col))

    def number(self, line, col):
        start = self.pos
        while self.peek() in DIGITS:
            self.advance()
        self.tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", self.source[start:self.pos], line, col))

    def word(self, line, col):
        start = self.pos
        while self.peek() in LETTERS or self.peek() in DIGITS:
            self.advance()
        text = self.source[start:self.pos]
        kind = "KEYWORD" if text in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
        self.tokens.append(Token(kind, text, line, col))

    def string(self, line, col):
        """A string literal. The token's text is the decoded value."""
        self.advance()  # the opening quote
        chars = []
        while True:
            ch = self.peek()
            if ch in ("", "\n"):
                # Strings never span lines, so the rest of this line is lost.
                self.errors.append(LexError("unterminated string", line, col))
                return
            if ch == '"':
                self.advance()
                break
            if ch == "\\":
                at_line, at_col = self.line, self.col
                self.advance()
                code = self.peek()
                if code in ESCAPES:
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[self.advance()])
                elif code not in ("", "\n"):
                    self.advance()
                    self.errors.append(LexError(f"unknown escape \\{code}", at_line, at_col))
                continue
            chars.append(self.advance())
        self.tokens.append(Token("STRING", "".join(chars), line, col))


def tokenize(source):
    """The tokens of source; raises the first LexError if there is one."""
    tokens, errors = Lexer(source).scan()
    if errors:
        raise errors[0]
    return tokens


def point_at(source, line, col):
    """Two lines: source line `line`, and a caret under column `col`.
    Tabs before the column are copied, so the caret lines up in a terminal."""
    lines = source.split("\n")
    text = lines[line - 1] if 1 <= line <= len(lines) else ""
    pad = "".join("\t" if c == "\t" else " " for c in text[:col - 1])
    return text + "\n" + pad.ljust(col - 1) + "^"


# ============================================================================
# The syntax tree
# ============================================================================

def pos_field():
    """A node's line or column: given by keyword, and never part of ==."""
    return field(default=0, kw_only=True, compare=False, repr=False)


@dataclass
class Node:
    line: int = pos_field()
    col: int = pos_field()


@dataclass
class Num(Node):
    value: int


@dataclass
class Str(Node):
    value: str


@dataclass
class Bool(Node):
    value: bool


@dataclass
class Nil(Node):
    pass


@dataclass
class Var(Node):
    name: str
    # How many scopes out the declaration is, or None for a global.
    # Filled in by the resolver.
    depth: object = field(default=None, kw_only=True, compare=False, repr=False)


@dataclass
class Unary(Node):
    op: str
    expr: Node


@dataclass
class Binary(Node):
    op: str
    left: Node
    right: Node


@dataclass
class Call(Node):
    callee: Node
    args: list


@dataclass
class Index(Node):
    target: Node
    index: Node


@dataclass
class ListLit(Node):
    items: list


@dataclass
class MapLit(Node):
    pairs: list     # (key, value) pairs of expressions


@dataclass
class FnExpr(Node):
    params: list    # (name, type) pairs; type is None without an annotation
    ret: object
    body: object    # a Block


@dataclass
class Let(Node):
    name: str
    type: object
    expr: Node


@dataclass
class Assign(Node):
    name: str
    expr: Node
    depth: object = field(default=None, kw_only=True, compare=False, repr=False)


@dataclass
class SetIndex(Node):
    target: Node
    index: Node
    expr: Node


@dataclass
class Print(Node):
    expr: Node


@dataclass
class If(Node):
    cond: Node
    then: object
    else_: object   # None, a Block, or an If (for "else if")


@dataclass
class While(Node):
    cond: Node
    body: object


@dataclass
class For(Node):
    name: str
    iterable: Node
    body: object


@dataclass
class Break(Node):
    pass


@dataclass
class Continue(Node):
    pass


@dataclass
class Fn(Node):
    name: str
    params: list
    ret: object
    body: object


@dataclass
class Return(Node):
    expr: object    # None for a bare "return;"


@dataclass
class ExprStmt(Node):
    expr: Node


@dataclass
class Block(Node):
    stmts: list


@dataclass
class Program(Node):
    stmts: list


# ============================================================================
# The parser
# ============================================================================

class ParseError(StaticError):
    """Tokens in an order the grammar does not allow."""


def describe(tok):
    """How a token is named in an error message."""
    if tok.kind == "EOF":
        return "end of input"
    if tok.kind == "STRING":
        return "a string"
    return f"'{tok.text}'"


# Binding powers, weakest first. An operator with a higher power takes its
# operands before an operator with a lower power does.
LOWEST, OR, AND, NOT, COMPARE, SUM, PRODUCT, UNARY, POSTFIX = range(9)
COMPARISONS = ("==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
INFIX = {
    "or": OR, "and": AND,
    "==": COMPARE, "!=": COMPARE, "<": COMPARE, "<=": COMPARE, ">": COMPARE, ">=": COMPARE,
    "+": SUM, "-": SUM,
    "*": PRODUCT, "/": PRODUCT, "%": PRODUCT,
    "(": POSTFIX, "[": POSTFIX,
}
STATEMENT_START = ("let", "fn", "if", "while", "for", "return", "print", "break", "continue")
TYPES = ("int", "bool", "str", "list", "map", "any")


class Parser:
    """A Pratt parser for expressions, and recursive descent for statements."""

    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0
        self.errors = []      # every ParseError found so far

    def peek(self):
        return self.tokens[self.pos]

    def at(self, *texts):
        """Is the next token one of these operators or keywords?"""
        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
        return tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") and tok.text in texts

    def advance(self):
        """Consumes the next token and returns it. EOF is never consumed."""
        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
        if tok.kind != "EOF":
            self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def error(self, message, tok=None):
        tok = tok or self.peek()
        return ParseError(message, tok.line, tok.col)

    def expect(self, text):
        if not self.at(text):
            raise self.error(f"expected '{text}', found {describe(self.peek())}")
        return self.advance()

    # ---- expressions: the Pratt loop -------------------------------------

    def expression(self, power=LOWEST):
        """An expression whose operators all bind more tightly than `power`."""
        left = self.prefix()
        while True:
            tok = self.peek()
            op_power = INFIX.get(tok.text, LOWEST) if tok.kind in ("OP", "KEYWORD") else LOWEST
            if op_power <= power:
                return left
            left = self.infix(left, op_power)

    def prefix(self):
        """Something that can start an expression."""
        tok = self.peek()
        where = dict(line=tok.line, col=tok.col)
        if tok.kind == "NUMBER":
            self.advance()
            return Num(int(tok.text), **where)
        if tok.kind == "STRING":
            self.advance()
            return Str(tok.text, **where)
        if tok.kind == "IDENT":
            self.advance()
            return Var(tok.text, **where)
        if self.at("true", "false"):
            self.advance()
            return Bool(tok.text == "true", **where)
        if self.at("nil"):
            self.advance()
            return Nil(**where)
        if self.at("-", "not"):
            self.advance()
            operand = self.expression(UNARY if tok.text == "-" else NOT)
            return Unary(tok.text, operand, **where)
        if self.at("("):
            self.advance()
            inner = self.expression()
            self.expect(")")
            return inner
        if self.at("["):
            self.advance()
            return ListLit(self.items("]"), **where)
        if self.at("{"):
            self.advance()
            return MapLit(self.pairs(), **where)
        if self.at("fn"):
            return self.function_expr()
        raise self.error(f"expected an expression, found {describe(tok)}")

    def infix(self, left, power):
        """An operator after a complete left operand, and what it needs after it."""
        tok = self.advance()
        where = dict(line=tok.line, col=tok.col)
        if tok.text == "(":
            return Call(left, self.items(")"), line=left.line, col=left.col)
        if tok.text == "[":
            index = self.expression()
            self.expect("]")
            return Index(left, index, **where)
        # A binary operator. The right side may only hold operators that bind
        # more tightly, so a second operator of the same power ends it: that
        # is what makes 10 - 3 - 2 group as (10 - 3) - 2.
        node = Binary(tok.text, left, self.expression(power), **where)
        if tok.text in COMPARISONS and self.at(*COMPARISONS):
            raise self.error("comparisons cannot be chained")
        return node

    def items(self, close):
        """Comma-separated expressions up to `close`, which is consumed."""
        items = []
        if not self.at(close):
            items.append(self.expression())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                items.append(self.expression())
        self.expect(close)
        return items

    def pairs(self):
        """The key: value pairs of a map literal, up to and including '}'."""
        pairs = []
        if not self.at("}"):
            pairs.append(self.pair())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                pairs.append(self.pair())
        self.expect("}")
        return pairs

    def pair(self):
        key = self.expression()
        self.expect(":")
        return (key, self.expression())

    # ---- statements, with error recovery ---------------------------------

    def program(self):
        """Every statement up to EOF. Errors are collected in self.errors and
        parsing goes on after each one, so one pass reports them all."""
        stmts = []
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            stmt = self.declaration()
            if stmt is not None:
                stmts.append(stmt)
        return Program(stmts)

    def declaration(self):
        """One statement. After a syntax error it records the error, skips to
        a safe place, and returns None."""
        start = self.pos
        try:
            return self.statement()
        except ParseError as e:
            self.errors.append(e)
            self.synchronize(start)
            return None

    def synchronize(self, start):
        """Panic mode: skip to just after a ';', or to a token that starts a
        statement, or to a '}' (so the block around us can close). A block
        entered while skipping is skipped whole, up to its own '}'. Always
        moves at least one token, so parsing cannot get stuck."""
        depth = 0
        if self.pos == start:
            depth = self.skip(depth)
        while self.peek().kind != "EOF":
            if depth == 0:
                before = self.tokens[self.pos - 1]
                if before.kind == "OP" and before.text == ";":
                    return
                if self.at(*STATEMENT_START) or self.at("}"):
                    return
            depth = self.skip(depth)

    def skip(self, depth):
        """Consumes one token while recovering; returns the new block depth."""
        tok = self.advance()
        if tok.kind == "OP" and tok.text == "{":
            return depth + 1
        if tok.kind == "OP" and tok.text == "}" and depth > 0:
            return depth - 1
        return depth

    def statement(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind == "KEYWORD":
            if tok.text == "fn" and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "IDENT":
                return self.fn_decl()
            handler = {
                "let": self.let_stmt, "print": self.print_stmt, "if": self.if_stmt,
                "while": self.while_stmt, "for": self.for_stmt, "return": self.return_stmt,
                "break": self.jump_stmt, "continue": self.jump_stmt,
            }.get(tok.text)
            if handler is not None:
                return handler()
        return self.simple_stmt()

    def end_statement(self):
        self.expect(";")

    def name(self):
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT":
            raise self.error(f"expected a name, found {describe(tok)}")
        return self.advance()

    def annotation(self, marker):
        """An optional type after ':' or '->'. Nothing checks types yet; they
        are notes for the reader."""
        if not self.at(marker):
            return None
        self.advance()
        tok = self.peek()
        if tok.kind != "IDENT" or tok.text not in TYPES:
            raise self.error(f"expected a type, found {describe(tok)}")
        return self.advance().text

    def let_stmt(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        type_ = self.annotation(":")
        self.expect("=")
        value = self.expression()
        self.end_statement()
        return Let(name.text, type_, value, line=name.line, col=name.col)

    def print_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        value = self.expression()
        self.end_statement()
        return Print(value, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def if_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        cond = self.expression()
        then = self.block()
        else_ = None
        if self.at("else"):
            self.advance()
            else_ = self.if_stmt() if self.at("if") else self.block()
        return If(cond, then, else_, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def while_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        cond = self.expression()
        return While(cond, self.block(), line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def for_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        self.expect("in")
        iterable = self.expression()
        return For(name.text, iterable, self.block(), line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def return_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        value = None if self.at(";") else self.expression()
        self.end_statement()
        return Return(value, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def jump_stmt(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        self.end_statement()
        kind = Break if tok.text == "break" else Continue
        return kind(line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def fn_decl(self):
        self.advance()
        name = self.name()
        params, ret, body = self.function_rest()
        return Fn(name.text, params, ret, body, line=name.line, col=name.col)

    def function_expr(self):
        tok = self.advance()
        params, ret, body = self.function_rest()
        return FnExpr(params, ret, body, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def function_rest(self):
        """What follows 'fn' or 'fn name': parameters, return type, body."""
        self.expect("(")
        params = []
        if not self.at(")"):
            params.append(self.param())
            while self.at(","):
                self.advance()
                params.append(self.param())
        self.expect(")")
        ret = self.annotation("->")
        return params, ret, self.block()

    def param(self):
        name = self.name()
        return (name.text, self.annotation(":"))

    def block(self):
        tok = self.expect("{")
        stmts = []
        while not self.at("}"):
            if self.peek().kind == "EOF":
                raise self.error(f"expected '}}' to close the block opened at {tok.line}:{tok.col}, "
                                 f"found end of input")
            stmt = self.declaration()
            if stmt is not None:
                stmts.append(stmt)
        self.advance()
        return Block(stmts, line=tok.line, col=tok.col)

    def simple_stmt(self):
        """An assignment (to a name or an index) or an expression statement."""
        expr = self.expression()
        if self.at("="):
            eq = self.advance()
            value = self.expression()
            self.end_statement()
            if isinstance(expr, Var):
                return Assign(expr.name, value, line=expr.line, col=expr.col)
            if isinstance(expr, Index):
                return SetIndex(expr.target, expr.index, value, line=expr.line, col=expr.col)
            # The statement itself was well formed, so report without panicking.
            self.errors.append(self.error("can only assign to a name or an index", eq))
            return None
        self.end_statement()
        return ExprStmt(expr, line=expr.line, col=expr.col)


def parse_expression(source):
    """One expression and nothing after it. Raises the first LexError or ParseError."""
    parser = Parser(tokenize(source))
    expr = parser.expression()
    if parser.peek().kind != "EOF":
        raise parser.error(f"expected end of input, found {describe(parser.peek())}")
    return expr


def parse(source):
    """(program, errors). If the lexer found mistakes, errors are the lexer's
    and program is None: parsing broken tokens only adds confusing errors.
    Otherwise errors are the parser's, and the program must not run unless
    there are none."""
    tokens, errors = Lexer(source).scan()
    if errors:
        return None, errors
    parser = Parser(tokens)
    program = parser.program()
    return program, parser.errors


def quote(text):
    """A string as Comet source writes it: in quotes, with its escapes."""
    return '"' + text.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n") + '"'


def group(head, *parts):
    return "(" + " ".join([head, *parts]) + ")"


def sexpr(node):
    """The tree as a prefix expression, for tests and debugging:
    1 + 2 * x becomes (+ 1 (* 2 x))."""
    if isinstance(node, Num):
        return str(node.value)
    if isinstance(node, Str):
        return quote(node.value)
    if isinstance(node, Bool):
        return "true" if node.value else "false"
    if isinstance(node, Nil):
        return "nil"
    if isinstance(node, Var):
        return node.name
    if isinstance(node, Unary):
        return group(node.op, sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, Binary):
        return group(node.op, sexpr(node.left), sexpr(node.right))
    if isinstance(node, Call):
        return group("call", sexpr(node.callee), *map(sexpr, node.args))
    if isinstance(node, Index):
        return group("index", sexpr(node.target), sexpr(node.index))
    if isinstance(node, ListLit):
        return group("list", *map(sexpr, node.items))
    if isinstance(node, MapLit):
        return group("map", *[sexpr(part) for pair in node.pairs for part in pair])
    return sexpr_statement(node)


def sexpr_statement(node):
    """sexpr for statements and functions: (let x 1), (block ...), ..."""
    if isinstance(node, (Fn, FnExpr)):
        params = "(" + " ".join(name for name, _type in node.params) + ")"
        head = ["fn", node.name] if isinstance(node, Fn) else ["fn"]
        return group(*head, params, sexpr(node.body))
    if isinstance(node, Let):
        return group("let", node.name, sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, Assign):
        return group("set", node.name, sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, SetIndex):
        return group("set", group("index", sexpr(node.target), sexpr(node.index)), sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, Print):
        return group("print", sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, ExprStmt):
        return group("expr", sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, If):
        parts = [sexpr(node.cond), sexpr(node.then)]
        if node.else_ is not None:
            parts.append(sexpr(node.else_))
        return group("if", *parts)
    if isinstance(node, While):
        return group("while", sexpr(node.cond), sexpr(node.body))
    if isinstance(node, For):
        return group("for", node.name, sexpr(node.iterable), sexpr(node.body))
    if isinstance(node, Break):
        return "(break)"
    if isinstance(node, Continue):
        return "(continue)"
    if isinstance(node, Return):
        return "(return)" if node.expr is None else group("return", sexpr(node.expr))
    if isinstance(node, Block):
        return group("block", *map(sexpr, node.stmts))
    if isinstance(node, Program):
        return group("program", *map(sexpr, node.stmts))
    raise TypeError(f"sexpr cannot show {type(node).__name__}")


# ============================================================================
# The resolver: names and jumps, checked before anything runs
# ============================================================================

class ResolveError(StaticError):
    """A name or a jump used where it cannot be."""


class Resolver:
    """Checks names and jumps before the program runs, and records on each
    Var and Assign how many scopes out the declaration is (None: a global).

    It walks the tree exactly the way the interpreter will, opening a scope
    wherever the interpreter makes an Environment: for a block, for a call
    (the parameters and the body share one), and for each pass of a for loop
    (the loop variable and the body share one)."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.scopes = []      # innermost last; name -> ready (False while its initializer runs)
        self.errors = []
        self.functions = 0    # how many fns we are inside
        self.loops = 0        # how many loops we are inside, within the innermost fn

    def resolve(self, node):
        getattr(self, "visit_" + type(node).__name__)(node)

    def resolve_all(self, nodes):
        for node in nodes:
            self.resolve(node)

    def error(self, message, node):
        self.errors.append(ResolveError(message, node.line, node.col))

    def declare(self, name, node):
        if not self.scopes:
            return   # a global: declaring it again replaces it, which a REPL needs
        scope = self.scopes[-1]
        if name in scope:
            self.error(f"{name} is already declared in this scope", node)
        scope[name] = False

    def define(self, name):
        if self.scopes:
            self.scopes[-1][name] = True

    def resolve_local(self, node, name):
        """Records how many scopes out `name` lives; None if in none of them."""
        for i in range(len(self.scopes) - 1, -1, -1):
            if name in self.scopes[i]:
                node.depth = len(self.scopes) - 1 - i
                return
        node.depth = None   # looked up in the globals when it runs

    def function(self, node):
        outer_loops = self.loops
        self.functions += 1
        self.loops = 0        # a break inside a fn cannot leave a loop outside it
        scope = {}
        for name, _type in node.params:
            if name in scope:
                self.error(f"duplicate parameter {name}", node)
            scope[name] = True
        self.scopes.append(scope)
        self.resolve_all(node.body.stmts)
        self.scopes.pop()
        self.functions -= 1
        self.loops = outer_loops

    # ---- statements ----

    def visit_Program(self, node):
        self.resolve_all(node.stmts)

    def visit_Block(self, node):
        self.scopes.append({})
        self.resolve_all(node.stmts)
        self.scopes.pop()

    def visit_Let(self, node):
        self.declare(node.name, node)
        self.resolve(node.expr)
        self.define(node.name)

    def visit_Assign(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.expr)
        self.resolve_local(node, node.name)

    def visit_SetIndex(self, node):
        self.resolve_all([node.target, node.index, node.expr])

    def visit_Print(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.expr)

    visit_ExprStmt = visit_Print

    def visit_If(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.cond)
        self.resolve(node.then)
        if node.else_ is not None:
            self.resolve(node.else_)

    def visit_While(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.cond)
        self.loops += 1
        self.resolve(node.body)
        self.loops -= 1

    def visit_For(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.iterable)
        self.loops += 1
        self.scopes.append({node.name: True})
        self.resolve_all(node.body.stmts)
        self.scopes.pop()
        self.loops -= 1

    def visit_Break(self, node):
        if self.loops == 0:
            self.error("break outside a loop", node)

    def visit_Continue(self, node):
        if self.loops == 0:
            self.error("continue outside a loop", node)

    def visit_Return(self, node):
        if self.functions == 0:
            self.error("return outside a function", node)
        if node.expr is not None:
            self.resolve(node.expr)

    def visit_Fn(self, node):
        self.declare(node.name, node)
        self.define(node.name)    # before the body, so the fn can call itself
        self.function(node)

    # ---- expressions ----

    def visit_FnExpr(self, node):
        self.function(node)

    def visit_Var(self, node):
        if self.scopes and self.scopes[-1].get(node.name) is False:
            self.error(f"cannot read {node.name} in its own initializer", node)
        self.resolve_local(node, node.name)

    def visit_Num(self, node):
        pass

    visit_Str = visit_Bool = visit_Nil = visit_Num

    def visit_Unary(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.expr)

    def visit_Binary(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.left)
        self.resolve(node.right)

    def visit_Call(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.callee)
        self.resolve_all(node.args)

    def visit_Index(self, node):
        self.resolve(node.target)
        self.resolve(node.index)

    def visit_ListLit(self, node):
        self.resolve_all(node.items)

    def visit_MapLit(self, node):
        for key, value in node.pairs:
            self.resolve(key)
            self.resolve(value)


def resolve(program):
    """Resolves every name in program; returns the list of ResolveErrors."""
    resolver = Resolver()
    resolver.resolve(program)
    return resolver.errors


# ============================================================================
# Values
# ============================================================================

class CometError(Exception):
    """A runtime error in the Comet program (not a bug in the interpreter)."""


def comet_div(a, b):
    """Integer division that rounds toward zero, like C."""
    if b == 0:
        raise CometError("division by zero")
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a < 0) == (b < 0) else -q


def comet_mod(a, b):
    return a - b * comet_div(a, b)


def type_name(value):
    """Comet's name for a value's type."""
    if value is None:
        return "nil"
    if isinstance(value, bool):     # before int: in Python, True is an int
        return "bool"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return "int"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return "str"
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return "list"
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return "map"
    if isinstance(value, (Closure, Builtin)):
        return "fn"
    raise TypeError(f"not a Comet value: {value!r}")


def repr_value(value):
    """A value as Comet source writes it: strings in quotes."""
    if value is None:
        return "nil"
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return str(value)
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return quote(value)
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return "[" + ", ".join(repr_value(item) for item in value) + "]"
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return "{" + ", ".join(f"{quote(k)}: {repr_value(v)}" for k, v in value.items()) + "}"
    if isinstance(value, Closure):
        return f"<fn {value.name}>" if value.name else "<fn>"
    if isinstance(value, Builtin):
        return f"<builtin {value.name}>"
    raise TypeError(f"not a Comet value: {value!r}")


def show(value):
    """What print writes: a string as it is, anything else as repr_value."""
    return value if isinstance(value, str) else repr_value(value)


def values_equal(a, b):
    """Comet's ==: values of different types are never equal."""
    if type_name(a) != type_name(b):
        return False
    if isinstance(a, list):
        return len(a) == len(b) and all(values_equal(x, y) for x, y in zip(a, b))
    if isinstance(a, dict):
        return a.keys() == b.keys() and all(values_equal(a[k], b[k]) for k in a)
    return a == b    # same Comet type, so Python's == is right (fns: the same fn)


ARITHMETIC = {
    "+": operator.add, "-": operator.sub, "*": operator.mul, "/": comet_div, "%": comet_mod,
    "<": operator.lt, "<=": operator.le, ">": operator.gt, ">=": operator.ge,
}
ORDERING = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=")
JOINABLE = ("str", "list")      # + also joins two of these (a new value)


def arithmetic(op, left, right):
    """+ - * / % < <= > >= with Comet's type rules."""
    lt, rt = type_name(left), type_name(right)
    if lt == rt == "int":
        return ARITHMETIC[op](left, right)
    if op == "+" and lt == rt and lt in JOINABLE:
        return left + right
    if op in ORDERING and lt == rt == "str":
        return ARITHMETIC[op](left, right)
    raise CometError(f"'{op}' cannot combine {lt} and {rt}")


class Closure:
    """A Comet function value: its declaration (an Fn or FnExpr node) and
    the Environment it was made in, which it keeps alive."""

    def __init__(self, decl, env):
        self.decl = decl
        self.env = env

    @property
    def name(self):
        return self.decl.name if isinstance(self.decl, Fn) else None

    def label(self):
        return self.name or "anonymous fn"


class ReturnSignal(Exception):
    """Carries a return value up to the call waiting for it. Not a
    CometError, so nothing a Comet program does can catch it."""

    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value


def check_arity(name, fewest, most, got):
    if fewest <= got <= most:
        return
    if fewest == most:
        wanted = f"{fewest} argument" + ("" if fewest == 1 else "s")
    elif most == fewest + 1:
        wanted = f"{fewest} or {most} arguments"
    else:
